steps: Cook brown rice: rinse dry rice with water. Cook in pot or rice cooker until fluffy (approx 35–40 min). Season with salt.
Dice onion and bell peppers. Mince garlic cloves.
Brown beef mince in a large oven-safe skillet or pot with olive oil over medium-high heat. Season with salt, pepper, onion powder, garlic powder, and paprika. Drain any excess fat.
Add onion and bell peppers to the beef. Cook 5 min until softened. Add minced garlic and cook 1 min.
Stir in diced tomatoes and beef broth. Simmer uncovered 10 min until slightly reduced.
Remove from heat. Fold in cooked rice and blended cottage cheese (blend smooth first for creaminess).
Transfer to a large baking dish. Bake at 180°C for 20 min until top is lightly golden.
Rest 5 min. Weigh total casserole, divide equally, and portion into containers.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Keeps 4 days refrigerated and freezes well for up to 3 months in individual portions; thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.
💡 Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth before folding it in, otherwise the curds separate in the oven and leave watery pockets. Reheat covered at 700 W for 3 minutes, stirring halfway.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Mix olive oil, minced garlic, lemon juice, rosemary, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Toss halved baby potatoes in half the herb oil. Spread on a baking tray. Roast 20 min.
Coat chicken breasts in remaining herb oil. Nestle around potatoes. Roast a further 25 min until breasts reach 74°C internally.
Steam or blanch green beans 4 min. Season with salt and pepper.
Weigh cooked chicken, divide equally. Portion thighs, potatoes, and green beans into containers.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled or freeze chicken and potatoes together for 2 months; reheat at 60–70% microwave power with a splash of water so the breast stays juicy rather than rubbery.
💡 Pull the breasts at 74°C on a probe rather than cooking to time; keep the green beans in a separate pot and add them cold to avoid grey, mushy beans.
subtitle: Skinless chicken breast · baby potatoes · green beans · garlic-herb · ~45 min

steps: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve baby potatoes and toss with olive oil, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Spread potatoes on a large baking tray. Roast 25 min, turning halfway.
Add cherry tomatoes and zucchini to the tray. Nestle cod fillets on top. Drizzle with remaining olive oil and lemon juice.
Return to oven for 14–16 min until cod is opaque and flakes easily.
Portion cod, potatoes, and vegetables across containers.
Squeeze remaining lemon over each portion. Refrigerate immediately.
💡 Cod dries out fast, so eat within 3 days and skip the freezer once cooked; reheat gently at 50% microwave power for 90 seconds, covered, or eat the flaked fish cold.
💡 Pat the fillets dry and add them to the tray only after the potatoes have had their 25 minutes, otherwise the fish overcooks while the potatoes are still firm.
subtitle: Cod fillet · baby potatoes · zucchini · cherry tomatoes · herbs · ~45 min

steps: Marinate chicken breasts in BBQ sauce and garlic powder for at least 30 min (overnight is better). Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Bake marinated chicken on a lined tray for 25–28 min until cooked through.
Cook brown rice: rinse dry rice with water in a pot or rice cooker. Season with salt.
Drain corn and black beans. Mix with diced tomatoes, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and a squeeze of lime.
Make high-protein ranch: mix Greek yogurt with garlic powder, onion powder, dried dill, salt, and pepper.
Rest chicken 5 min, then slice. Weigh and divide equally across containers.
Layer rice, corn-bean salsa, and sliced BBQ chicken in each container.
Add a dollop of Greek yogurt ranch on top. Drizzle with olive oil. Seal and refrigerate.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
name: 🍗 🇺🇸 BBQ Chicken & Corn Rice Bowl

steps: Cook brown rice.
Brown beef mince. Season well. Drain ALL excess fat — critical for macro accuracy.
Sauté diced bell peppers and add to beef.
Blend sour cream, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, Président Light mozzarella, chipotle peppers and lime juice until smooth.
Portion rice into containers. Top with beef-pepper mix and drizzle sauce. Finish with a sprinkle of parmesan. mist the pan with cooking spray.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.

steps: Cube potatoes evenly. Season with salt, pepper, rosemary. Spray with PAM only. Roast 200°C for 35–40 min, turn halfway.
Brown beef mince in a pan. Season well. Drain all excess fat before portioning.
Slice veg. Air fry at 190°C for 15 min or roast last 20 min alongside potatoes.
Portion: beef · white potato · sweet potato · mixed veg.
No oil needed — use a non-stick pan throughout.
💡 Keeps 5 days refrigerated and freezes well for 3 months; reheat from chilled at full power for 3 minutes, stirring the mince halfway so it heats evenly.
💡 Cut white and sweet potato into cubes of the same size and spread them in a single layer; crowded trays steam rather than roast and you lose the crisp edges.
subtitle: Lean mince · white & sweet potato · roasted veg · ~60 min

steps: Brown beef with garlic powder and paprika. Add onion halfway. Drain excess fat.
Cook pasta separately. Drain.
Mix the Big Mac sauce cold: 210 g 0% Greek yogurt, 105 g sweet relish, 28 g sugar-free ketchup, 14 g yellow mustard. Whisk until smooth.

Take the beef off the heat and let it cool 5 min. Combine the beef, pasta, chopped tomatoes, baby spinach, and sliced dill pickles, then fold the sauce through the whole batch — hot beef splits the yogurt.
Divide into containers.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.

steps: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with chipotle chilli powder, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high. Sear chicken in batches until golden. Remove and set aside. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
In the same pot, sauté diced onion 3 min until softened, then garlic 1 min. Add pumpkin cubes and cook 3 min.
Add diced tomatoes, broth, chipotle, and corn. Stir to combine. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to pot. Add drained black beans. Simmer uncovered 20 min until pumpkin is tender.
Taste and adjust seasoning — more chipotle for heat, a splash of lime juice for brightness.
Weigh total chilli, divide equally, and portion into containers.
Serve with optional low-fat sour cream or plain Greek yogurt on top (not included in macros).
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Add chicken, Frank's Red Hot Sauce and ranch dressing to slow cooker. Cook HIGH 3hr. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Cook pasta al dente. Drain. Cook beef bacon until crispy, crumble.
Shred chicken. Add pasta, bacon, diced celery, baby spinach, cottage cheese and Président Light mozzarella. Mix well.
Top each portion with a sprinkle of parmesan. Divide into containers.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.

steps: Season beef with onion powder, paprika, and garlic powder. Cook in a large skillet until fully browned.
Make the sauce: mix the light mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard, and a splash of pickle juice in a bowl.
Dice onions and shred lettuce. Set aside.
Lay out tortillas. Distribute beef, diced onion, pickle slices, and sauce evenly among them.
Place a slice of cheese on each tortilla.
Fold both ends in, then roll tightly to form burritos.
Toast burritos on a lightly oiled skillet over medium-high heat until golden on both sides.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Dice chicken into 2cm cubes. Season with paprika, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high. Cook chicken cubes 8–10 min until golden and cooked through. Set aside. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
In the same pan, cook diced onion and garlic 3 min. Add canned tomatoes and simmer 5 min.
Add cauliflower rice to the pan. Stir-fry 5–6 min until tender.
Add baby spinach and stir until wilted (1–2 min). Return chicken and mix everything together.
Weigh total, divide equally, portion into containers.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.

steps: Dice onion, carrots, and celery. Mince garlic. Rinse lentils well.
Set Instant Pot to Sauté. Cook onion, garlic, carrot, and celery in a spray of oil for 5 min.
Add canned tomatoes, lentils, chicken broth, turmeric, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Stir well.
Nestle whole chicken breasts into the pot. Seal and pressure cook on High for 12 min. Natural release 10 min. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Remove chicken, shred with two forks, return to pot. Stir in spinach until wilted.
Adjust seasoning. Portion soup into containers — lentils continue to thicken overnight, which is normal.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Chicken breast · red lentils · carrots · celery · turmeric-cumin broth · ~30 min + overnight

steps: Add chicken, the jar of Alfredo sauce, the jar of Italian tomato sauce, and garlic to slow cooker. Cook HIGH 3hr. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Cook pasta al dente. Drain.

Shred chicken. Add sliced mushrooms and baby spinach to the slow cooker; cook 10 min more. Stir in cottage cheese and Président Light mozzarella until smooth. Add pasta and broccoli florets. Cook 15 min more.
Divide into containers. Top with parmesan.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Slow-cooked chicken · Alfredo · Italian tomato sauce · cottage cheese · ~3 h 20 min

steps: Sauté diced peppers and onion. Add to slow cooker with chicken, buffalo sauce and seasonings. Cook HIGH 2hr. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Blend cottage cheese, cream cheese, Président Light mozzarella, parmesan, milk and honey for 4–5 min until smooth.
Cook pasta al dente. Cook beef bacon until crispy, chop.
Shred chicken. Add pasta, cheese sauce and bacon. Cook 30 min more.
Divide into containers.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Chicken · beef bacon · pasta · blended cottage cheese sauce · ~2 h 20 min

steps: Season the chicken breasts with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Heat a skillet over medium-high, spray with oil. Sauté onion, garlic, and mushrooms until golden, about 5 min. Set aside.
In the same pan, cook the chicken until fully done, about 6-7 min per side. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
In a bowl, mix Greek yogurt, Dijon mustard, and espresso. Season with salt and pepper.
Turn off heat. Return mushroom mix to pan. Pour sauce over everything and stir — residual heat thickens the sauce.
Finish with fresh parsley. Serve with rice or roasted veg.
🌅 Morning-only meal: this recipe contains a double espresso. Consuming it in the afternoon or evening may disrupt sleep. Swap espresso for decaf if making this as a later meal.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Mushroom cream · Stovetop · ~25 min

steps: Preheat oven to 220°C. Drain and rinse chickpeas. Pat dry with a paper towel — this is key for crispness.
Toss chickpeas, capsicum, zucchini, and red onion with olive oil, harissa, salt, and pepper on a large baking tray. Spread in a single layer.
Roast 30 min, tossing once halfway, until vegetables are caramelised and chickpeas are slightly crisp.
While veg roasts, place dry couscous in a large bowl. Pour hot vegetable broth over it (1:1.2 ratio). Cover tightly with cling wrap and rest 5 min. Fluff with a fork.
Add lemon juice and chopped parsley to the couscous and toss to combine.
Mix roasted chickpeas and vegetables through the couscous.
Portion into containers. Add a dollop of Greek yogurt and a spoonful of cottage cheese to each portion. Add fresh cucumber when serving for crunch.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.

🔬 Leucine note: chickpeas are a solid plant protein but fall short of the 2.5g leucine threshold per meal that triggers muscle protein synthesis. Greek yogurt + cottage cheese here bridges that gap — science-backed, not just filler.
💡 Keep the cucumber, yogurt and cottage cheese in a separate pot and add them cold; the couscous base keeps 4 days but goes limp with wet dairy sitting on it.
💡 Eat this cold or at room temperature; if you do warm it, 90 seconds at 600 W is plenty, as the roasted chickpeas lose their crunch quickly. Do not freeze, as the couscous turns mushy.
subtitle: Chickpeas · roasted capsicum · zucchini · couscous · harissa · ~50 min

steps: Blend chipotle peppers, garlic, lime juice and stock until smooth.
Pour into slow cooker. Add chicken. Cook HIGH 3hr. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Cook rice in remaining stock.
Drain excess liquid. Shred chicken. Stir in drained black beans. Blend cottage cheese and light mozz into sauce.
Portion rice into containers. Top with chicken, corn+pico mix, and sour cream. Sprinkle parmesan over each. mist the pan with cooking spray.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Blended chipotle · rice · corn · pico · Daisy sour cream · ~3 h 20 min

steps: Cook brown rice: rinse, then cook dry rice with water in rice cooker or pot until tender. Season with salt.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Line two baking sheets with parchment.
Slice chicken breasts to even portions. Season with garlic powder, salt, paprika, and a squeeze of lemon.
Toss broccoli florets with olive oil, salt, pepper, and minced garlic.
Bake chicken 22–25 min until internal temp reaches 74°C. Roast broccoli on second tray 18–20 min.
Weigh total cooked chicken, divide equally. Portion rice, chicken, and broccoli into containers. Add halved cherry tomatoes to each.
Finish each container with a squeeze of fresh lemon and a sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Pull the chicken at 74°C on the thickest piece and rest it before slicing; even 5 degrees over turns breast dry and stringy after a second heating.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled. Reheat at 600 W for 2 to 3 minutes with a splash of water over the rice, and add the parsley and lemon squeeze after heating so they stay bright.
subtitle: Chicken breast · jasmine rice · broccoli · garlic-lemon · ~45 min

steps: Season steak generously with salt and lightly with pepper. Rest on a wire rack while you prep the rest (or cook immediately).
Heat a large non-stick pot or Dutch oven over high heat (no oil needed). Sear steak 4–6 min per side until deeply browned — work in batches if needed. Rest on a cutting board.
In the same pot, add diced onions. Deglaze with a splash of water, scraping up all the brown bits. Cook until onions are soft and browned.
Add black pepper, thyme, garlic powder, and beef bone broth. Reduce until syrupy, about 15–20 min.
Cook penne al dente; drain. Dice the rested steak into bite-sized cubes.
Blend cream cheese, evaporated milk, and cottage cheese until completely smooth. Reduce heat to low heat; whisk the blended cream sauce into the pot.
Add drained pasta, diced steak, sliced mushrooms, baby spinach, halved cherry tomatoes, and parmesan. Mix well. Fold in Gruyère.
Cover and cook on low heat 10–15 min until sauce thickens. Portion into containers.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Form the ground chicken into equal-sized balls. Season with salt, pepper, paprika, and garlic powder. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Beat the eggs in a bowl. Add a few drops of Tabasco for a spicy version.
Put Corn Flakes in a zip-lock bag and crush into coarse crumbs. Spread on a plate.
Dip each chicken ball into beaten egg, then roll in crushed Corn Flakes, pressing to coat evenly.
Spray the air fryer basket with the cooking oil spray and mist the coated nuggets lightly on top. Air fry at 180°C for 25–30 minutes until golden and crispy and internal temp reaches 75°C.
Serve with a dipping sauce — Greek yogurt mixed with Dijon mustard and garlic powder works perfectly. (optional — not counted in the macros)
💡 Store nuggets 4 days chilled or freeze on a tray before bagging; reheat in the air fryer at 190°C for 5–6 minutes, never the microwave, or the cornflake crust goes soft.
💡 Press the crushed cornflakes firmly onto each ball and leave space between them in the basket so the coating dries out and crisps rather than steaming.
Preheat oven to 190°C. Toss halved baby potatoes with salt, pepper, garlic, and a spray of water. Line tray with baking paper. Roast 25–30 min until golden.
Dice onion and bell pepper. Sauté in a non-stick oven-safe pan until softened — 5 min. Add garlic, cook 1 min more.
Add spinach and stir until wilted. Remove from heat.
Whisk egg whites and whole eggs together. Season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of paprika. Stir in crumbled feta.
Pour egg mixture over the vegetables in the pan. Bake at 190°C for 20–22 min until set and lightly golden.
Cool, cut frittata into portions. Serve each with a portion of roasted potatoes.
💡 The frittata keeps 4 days chilled and freezes in individual wedges for a month; reheat at 50% microwave power for 2 minutes so the egg whites do not turn spongy.
💡 Squeeze excess liquid from the wilted spinach before pouring in the eggs, otherwise water pools under the frittata and the base never sets properly.
subtitle: Liquid egg whites · whole eggs · baby potatoes · spinach · pepper · ~50 min

steps: Slow cooker: add chicken, garlic, Dijon, Worcestershire, stock, thyme, and seasonings. Cook HIGH 3hr. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Caramelize the onions in butter + remaining stock over medium heat until dark brown (~45 min).
Blend fat-free cottage cheese, Président Light mozzarella, parmesan, milk and ¾ caramelized onions until smooth.
Cook pasta al dente. Drain.
Shred chicken. Add pasta, sliced mushrooms, baby spinach, cheese sauce, and remaining onions. Mix well. Divide into containers.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Chicken · caramelized onions · cottage cheese & parmesan sauce · ~3 h 20 min

steps: Add chicken, cream cheese, cottage cheese, Président Light mozzarella, garlic and milk to slow cooker. Cook HIGH 3hr. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Cook pasta al dente. Steam broccoli separately.
Shred chicken. Add pasta, broccoli, sun-dried tomatoes and parmesan. Cook 15 min more.
Divide into containers.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Chicken · broccoli · garlic parmesan & cream cheese sauce · ~3 h 20 min

steps: Cook brown rice in rice cooker (brown rice needs 1.25× water ratio and ~35 min).
Slice peppers and zucchini into thin strips. Mince garlic and grate ginger.
Pat shrimp dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat a large wok or pan over high heat. Add the sesame oil. Stir-fry shrimp 2 min per side until pink. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, stir-fry vegetables with garlic and ginger for 4–5 min until tender-crisp.
Return shrimp to pan, add soy sauce and snap peas. Toss 1 min.
Weigh total stir-fry, divide equally. Portion with brown rice into containers.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.

💡 Shrimp tighten and go rubbery when reheated hard, so warm these portions gently at 50 percent power in 60-second bursts until just hot. They keep 3 days in the fridge and are best not frozen once cooked.
💡 Cook the shrimp in two batches so the wok stays searing hot; overcrowding drops the temperature and they boil in their own liquid instead of browning.
subtitle: Shrimp · brown rice · snap peas · bell pepper · sesame-ginger · ~55 min

steps: Marinate chicken in lemon juice, minced garlic, dried oregano, salt, and pepper for at least 30 min.
Preheat oven to 200°C or heat grill pan. Cook chicken 22–25 min until 74°C internally. Rest and slice.
Cook orzo in boiling salted water until al dente (~9 min). Drain and cool slightly.
Dice cucumber. Halve tomatoes. Halve olives.
Toss orzo with cucumber, tomatoes, olives, feta, lemon juice, .
Weigh sliced chicken, divide equally. Portion over orzo salad in containers.
💡 Best eaten cold within 4 days; do not freeze, as the cucumber and tomato turn watery. If you want it warm, reheat only the chicken and put it back over the cold salad.
💡 Rinse the drained orzo briefly under cold water and toss it with lemon juice while still warm, which stops it clumping into one solid block in the container.
subtitle: Chicken breast · orzo · cucumber · tomato · olives · lemon-herb · ~45 min

steps: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli and capsicum with garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray and roast 25 min until golden.
Cook quinoa: rinse, then simmer in water or veggie broth for 15 min until fluffy. Fluff with a fork.

Whisk eggs with a pinch of salt. In a non-stick pan over low heat-medium heat, add a small knob of butter and scramble eggs very slowly — pull them off heat while still slightly glossy for the best texture.
Stir cottage cheese into the warm scrambled eggs off heat. The residual heat will warm the cottage cheese without curdling it.
Wilt kale or spinach in the same pan for 2 min with a splash of water.
Divide quinoa into containers. Layer roasted veg, then egg-cottage cheese mixture, then wilted greens.
Top each container with crumbled feta or Parmesan. Refrigerate — eat within 3 days for best egg texture.
💡 Eat within 3 days and do not freeze, as scrambled egg and cottage cheese both weep liquid when thawed; reheat at 50% power for 90 seconds or eat the egg layer cold.
💡 Pull the eggs off the heat while still glossy and stir the cottage cheese in off the heat, otherwise reheating later tips them from soft curds into rubber.
subtitle: Scrambled eggs · cottage cheese · roasted veggies · quinoa · ~45 min

steps: Add the chicken, the 500 g light creamy pasta sauce, and the 400 g tomato spaghetti sauce to the slow cooker. Cook HIGH 3 hr. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Sauté the diced peppers, onion, and 10 g garlic in the butter and stock until golden. Add to the slow cooker.
Blend fat-free cottage cheese and stir into slow cooker for extra protein.
Par-cook pasta for half the package time. Drain. Add to slow cooker. Cook HIGH 30 min more.
Divide into containers. Top with parmesan.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Chicken · sautéed green peppers · creamy + tomato sauce · ~3 h 20 min

steps: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pierce sweet potatoes and bake whole for 45–55 min until fully soft.
Season steaks generously with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and a touch of smoked paprika.
Heat a cast iron or heavy skillet over high heat until smoking. Sear steaks 3–4 min per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Rest 5 min.
Roast broccoli florets tossed in olive oil, salt, and pepper at 200°C for 18–20 min alongside.
Scoop sweet potato flesh, mash with light butter, a splash of broth, garlic powder, salt, and pepper until smooth.
Make the yogurt-based steak sauce: mix Greek yogurt with Worcestershire sauce, Dijon mustard, garlic, salt.
Slice steaks thin against the grain. Weigh and divide across containers.
Plate sweet potato mash, broccoli, and steak slices. Drizzle with yogurt steak sauce and pan juices.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Cook brown rice in rice cooker.
Dice onion, bell peppers, and mince garlic.

Heat the 7 g olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Brown the turkey mince 8–10 min. Season with cumin, chilli powder, garlic powder, paprika, and salt. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Add onion, garlic, and peppers. Cook 5 min.
Add canned tomatoes and drained black beans. Simmer 8–10 min.
Portion the rice and turkey-bean mixture across the containers. Cut the 2 limes into wedges and squeeze one over each portion at serving.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Turkey mince · jasmine rice · black beans · salsa · cumin · ~30 min + chill

steps: Score lamb leg and push garlic slivers into the cuts. Rub with rosemary, salt, pepper, and lemon zest.
Roast lamb at 190°C for 45–55 min (medium). Rest 10 min before slicing. Aim for 74°C internal for well-done.
Cook quinoa: rinse dry quinoa, cook 1:2 with water ~15 min until fluffy. Season with salt.
Snap woody ends off asparagus. Roast on a baking-paper-lined tray, seasoned with salt, at 200°C for 12–15 min.
Blend the cottage cheese smooth, then mix with Greek yogurt, chopped mint, a squeeze of lemon, and a pinch of salt for the tzatziki-style sauce. Keep it cold until serving.
Slice lamb evenly. Weigh and divide across containers with quinoa and asparagus.
Crumble feta and add a dollop of mint yogurt sauce over each container.
Drizzle with remaining lemon juice before sealing. Best consumed within 4 days.
💡 Sliced lamb keeps 4 days and freezes for 2 months without the sauce; reheat lamb and quinoa at 60% power for 2 minutes, then add the mint yogurt cold from a separate pot.
💡 Rest the lamb the full 10 minutes before slicing thinly across the grain; carving straight from the oven pushes the juices out onto the board.
Cook brown rice the night before and refrigerate — cold rice is essential for fried rice.
Cut steak into bite-sized cubes. Season with salt, pepper, and a splash of soy sauce. Set aside.
Heat a large skillet over high heat. Add the sesame oil, then cold rice, sliced zucchini, sliced mushrooms, and diced onion. Stir-fry for 5–10 mins. Add soy sauce and toss to coat.
Push rice to the edges. Crack eggs into the centre and scramble until cooked, then mix into the rice.
Remove rice from pan. Sear steak cubes over high heat until medium-rare (130–60°C internal).
Mix the yum-yum sauce cold: 105 g light mayonnaise, Frank's Red Hot to taste, and a squeeze of lime. Keep it out of the hot pan — it goes on at portioning.
Combine steak, rice, and veg in a large bowl. Weigh, divide equally, and distribute sauce per container.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.

Season chicken breasts generously with Italian herb seasoning, minced garlic, a squeeze of lemon juice, salt, and black pepper on both sides. Spray lightly with a light mist of cooking spray. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Air fry at 200°C for 18–20 min, flipping halfway. Check internal temp reaches 75°C. Rest 3 min, then slice or dice.
Cook rice in a rice cooker or pot (1:1.5 rice to water ratio). Fluff with a fork when done.

Cut salmon into cubes. Season with salt, pepper, garlic powder.
Air fry at 180°C for 15–20 min, stirring halfway, until golden and cooked through.
In a bowl: combine chopped avocado, sliced red onion, feta cubed small. Add cooked salmon.
Make the sauce: mix yogurt, lemon juice, salt, pepper, garlic powder. Pour over bowl and mix.
Place the mixture in the centre of the wrap. Fold sides in, roll tightly.
Air fry at 180°C for 10 min flipping halfway until wrap is golden and crispy. Serve immediately.
💡 This burrito is made to be eaten within the hour; chill the salmon-avocado filling for up to 2 days and roll and crisp the wrap fresh, since a stored wrap goes leathery.
💡 Drain excess yogurt sauce off the filling before rolling and tuck the ends in tightly; a wet filling soaks through the wrap and it splits in the air fryer.
subtitle: Crispy wrap · Air fryer · ~40 min

steps: Cook quinoa: rinse, then simmer quinoa in water for 15 min. Fluff and cool.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking sheet.
Pat salmon fillets dry. Season with olive oil, garlic, lemon zest, salt and pepper.
Snap woody ends off asparagus. Toss with oil, salt, and pepper.
Place salmon skin-down on the baking sheet. Add asparagus alongside. Roast 14–16 min until salmon flakes easily.
Portion quinoa, one salmon fillet, and asparagus spears into containers. Garnish with fresh dill and lemon wedge.
💡 Keeps 3 days refrigerated; salmon reheats best at 50% microwave power for 60–90 seconds under a damp paper towel, or flake it cold through the quinoa as a salad.
💡 Roast skin-side down on the lined sheet; the skin shields the flesh from the tray heat and peels away cleanly once the fish has cooled, leaving neat fillets for portioning.
subtitle: Salmon fillet · quinoa · asparagus · lemon-garlic · ~35 min

steps: Cook quinoa: rinse, simmer in water for 15 min. Cool to room temperature.
Make tabbouleh: finely chop parsley, dice cucumber and tomatoes, slice spring onions. Mix with quinoa, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Season tuna steaks generously with salt, pepper, and a little olive oil.
Heat a heavy pan or grill pan over very high heat. Sear tuna 90 seconds per side for rare, or 2.5 min per side for cooked through.
Rest 2 min. Slice or leave whole.
Portion quinoa tabbouleh into containers. Add tuna. Serve with lemon wedge.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Yellowfin tuna steak · quinoa · parsley · cucumber · lemon · ~35 min

steps: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pierce sweet potatoes, bake whole for 45–55 min until tender. Cool, then peel and cube.
Bring steaks to room temperature 30 min before cooking. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat. Sear steaks 3–4 min per side for medium. Rest 5 min, then slice thin.
Dice cucumbers and red onion. Halve tomatoes. Mix into a bowl with lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Portion sliced steak, sweet potato cubes, and cucumber salad across containers.
Drizzle any resting juices from the steak over each container before sealing.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Sirloin · sweet potato · cucumber · red onion · lemon dressing · ~75 min

steps: Add chicken breast to slow cooker. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Pour in honey, both soy sauces, hoisin sauce, rice wine vinegar, and chicken stock.
Add crushed ginger, diced onion, and chopped spring onion.
Cook on low for 6 hours (or high for 3 hours).
Add snow peas and sliced capsicum in the last 30 minutes.
Stir in cashews just before serving. Shred or slice the chicken.
Serve over jasmine rice — macros shown are without rice, add ~130 kcal / 27C per cooked rice.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Keep the cashews in a small bag and scatter them on after reheating; stored in the sauce they go soft and chalky within a day.
💡 The chicken and sauce keep 4 days in the fridge and freeze well for 3 months without the snow peas, which go grey and limp once frozen. Reheat covered at 700 W for 2 to 3 minutes.
Dice onion and cube sweet potatoes. Mince garlic.
In a slow cooker, add chicken breasts, broth, passata, onion, garlic, diced bell pepper, smoked paprika, cumin, garlic powder, and chilli powder.
Cook on Low 6–8 hours or High 3–4 hours until chicken shreds easily. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Remove chicken and shred with two forks. Return to the cooker. Stir in corn kernels and baby spinach; cook 5 min until spinach wilts and corn is warmed through.
Cook brown rice in rice cooker. Steam or bake sweet potato cubes separately.
Weigh pulled chicken mixture, divide equally. Portion with rice and sweet potato into containers.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Chicken breast · jasmine rice · sweet potato · BBQ spice rub · broth · ~3 h 20 min + chill

steps: Season turkey breast generously with salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and dried thyme.
Place turkey, squash cubes, garlic cloves, and broth into slow cooker. Cook LOW 4 hr or HIGH 2.5 hr. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Meanwhile, steam or blanch green beans until just tender, about 5 min. Season with salt and pepper.
Blend cottage cheese with a splash of broth until smooth — this is your 'gravy' sauce.
Once turkey is cooked, shred or slice. Weigh and divide across containers.
Add butternut squash, green beans, and cottage cheese gravy sauce to each container.
Finish each portion with cranberry sauce. Drizzle olive oil over the top.
Seal containers. Reheat uncovered 2–3 min in microwave, adding water if needed.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Cook brown rice: rinse dry rice, cook 1:2.5 with water for ~35 min. Season with salt.
Rinse canned/cooked lentils. If using dry lentils, boil dry lentils ~20 min until tender.
Caramelise the onions: slice thin, cook in a non-stick pan (no oil) over low heat-medium heat for 25–30 min, stirring often until dark golden. This is the key flavour step.
Brown lamb mince in a non-stick pan. Add garlic and baharat (or a mix of allspice, cinnamon, cumin, coriander). Season generously.
Stir tomato paste into lamb mince. Add cooked lentils and a splash of water. Simmer 10 min.
Combine lamb-lentil mix with brown rice. Fold in half the caramelised onions.
Divide into containers. Top each with remaining caramelised onions.
Serve with a dollop of plain Greek yogurt (per portion included in macros).

🎉 This is a special occasion recipe — richer macros than a standard SoulGainz main are intentional. To boost protein closer to 50 g, add an extra 100 g Greek yogurt per portion (+10 g protein, +65 kcal).
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Bake whole sweet potato for 45 min until completely soft. Allow to cool slightly.
Reduce oven to 180°C.
Place the soft sweet potato in a 23 cm baking dish and smash it flat with a fork to cover the base evenly.
Layer sliced zucchini, chopped asparagus, and halved cherry tomatoes over the sweet potato base.
Crack the eggs over the vegetables. Dollop cottage cheese around the dish. Sprinkle with Parmesan and season with salt and pepper.
Bake 30 min until eggs are set and the top is golden. Slice into portions.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled; freeze individual slices wrapped tightly for a month and reheat at 50% power for 2–3 minutes so the eggs warm through without splitting.
💡 Salt the zucchini slices and blot them for 10 minutes before layering, otherwise their water floods the smashed sweet potato base and the eggs set in a puddle.
Cook brown rice in rice cooker. Cook edamame in boiling water 4 min, drain.
Slice chicken into strips. Season with salt and pepper.
Make teriyaki sauce: combine soy sauce, honey, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch mixed with cold water.
Cook chicken in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat until cooked through — 6–8 min. Set aside. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Blanch broccoli, snap peas, and bok choy 3 min. Drain.
Return chicken to pan, pour teriyaki sauce over. Toss on medium heat until sauce thickens and coats chicken — 2 min.
Portion rice, teriyaki chicken, broccoli, snap peas, bok choy, and edamame across containers.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Mix the cornstarch into cold water until fully dissolved before it goes anywhere near the hot pan, otherwise it seizes into lumps and the glaze never thickens evenly.
💡 The cornstarch glaze thickens further in the fridge, so add 15 ml of water before microwaving at 700 W for 2 to 3 minutes. Keeps 4 days; freeze the chicken and rice but not the bok choy.
subtitle: Chicken breast · jasmine rice · edamame · broccoli · teriyaki glaze · ~30 min

steps: Press tofu for at least 30 min (or overnight wrapped in a towel with a heavy pan on top). Cut into 2cm cubes.
Cook brown rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Heat the sesame oil in a large non-stick pan over high heat. Add tofu cubes — do not move them for 3–4 min until a golden crust forms. Flip and brown all sides. Remove from pan.
In the same pan, sauté garlic 1 min. Add broccoli florets and stir-fry 4 min until bright green and tender-crisp.
Add edamame and cook 2 min until heated through.
Return tofu to the pan. Pour teriyaki sauce and soy sauce over everything. Toss to coat and cook 2 min until sauce thickens.
Portion rice into containers, top with tofu/veggie mix, and sprinkle sesame seeds. Add a spoonful of cottage cheese to each portion.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.

🔬 Leucine note: tofu and edamame are the best plant sources of leucine, but still sit just below the 2.5g threshold needed to maximally trigger muscle protein synthesis. The cottage cheese in this recipe closes that gap — don't skip it.
subtitle: Firm tofu · edamame · broccoli · teriyaki sauce · jasmine rice · ~25 min + overnight

steps: Drain and rinse chickpeas. Drain tuna and break into chunks.
Dice cucumbers, halve cherry tomatoes, thinly slice red onion.
Make dressing: combine lemon juice, olive oil, salt, pepper, and chopped parsley. Whisk well.
In a large bowl, combine chickpeas, tuna, cucumber, tomatoes, and red onion.
Pour dressing over and toss to coat.
Portion into containers. Keep dressing separate if prepping more than 3 days ahead.
💡 Keeps 3 days refrigerated with the dressing on, or 4 if dressed on the day; never freeze, as the cucumber turns to water and the chickpeas go mealy.
💡 Slice the red onion paper-thin and soak it in the lemon juice for 10 minutes before mixing, which softens the raw bite that otherwise dominates by day two.
subtitle: Canned tuna · chickpeas · cucumber · tomato · lemon-olive oil · ~10 min

steps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a 30×20cm baking dish.
Dice capsicum. Steam or microwave broccoli 3 min until just tender. Halve cherry tomatoes.
Sauté minced garlic and capsicum in a non-stick pan 2–3 min. Add spinach and stir until wilted. Set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk together all the eggs and cottage cheese until smooth. Season generously with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Stir in sautéed vegetables, broccoli florets, and half the feta.
Pour mixture into the greased baking dish. Scatter remaining feta and cherry tomatoes on top.
Bake 30–35 min until centre is fully set and top is lightly golden. Test with a skewer — it should come out clean.
Cool 10 min before slicing into equal portions. Store in airtight containers.
💡 Slices keep 4 days in the fridge and freeze for a month between sheets of baking paper; reheat at 60% microwave power for 90 seconds or eat cold on the go.
💡 Steam the broccoli and sauté the capsicum first as written; raw vegetables release water during the bake and leave a soggy layer at the bottom of the dish.
subtitle: Eggs · cottage cheese · feta · roasted veg · ~55 min

steps: Heat olive oil in a large, wide pan over medium heat. Sauté diced onion 5 min until softened.
Add diced red pepper and minced garlic. Cook 3 min. Add cumin, paprika, and chili flakes — stir 1 min.
Add crushed tomatoes and drained chickpeas. Stir well. Simmer 10–12 min until sauce thickens.
Add fresh spinach and stir until wilted. Season with salt and pepper.
Make a well for each egg in the sauce using a spoon. Crack one egg into each well.
Cover pan and cook on low heat 6–8 min until whites are set but yolks still slightly runny. For meal prep, cook yolks through (8–10 min).
Remove from heat. Dollop the cottage cheese over the sauce between the eggs, off the heat so it stays creamy, then crumble feta over the top.
Portion equal eggs + sauce into each container. Serve with wholegrain pita or rice cakes.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Eggs · chickpeas · spiced tomato sauce · ~30 min

steps: Cook pasta al dente according to package. Reserve pasta water before draining.

Blend cottage cheese, grated parmesan, skimmed milk, lemon juice and zest, salt, and pepper until completely smooth. This is your cream sauce. (optional — not counted in the macros) heat a non-stick pan with a light mist of cooking spray in a large pan over medium. Add minced garlic and chili flakes — cook 1–2 min until fragrant.
Add drained white beans. Stir and cook 2–3 min until lightly golden.
Add baby spinach in handfuls, stirring until wilted (~2 min).
Add cooked pasta and cream sauce. Toss everything together. Use reserved pasta water to loosen if needed. (optional — not counted in the macros)
Taste and adjust seasoning. Simmer 1–2 min to meld flavours.
Portion into containers. Add extra parmesan on top if desired. Reheat with a splash of water.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.

🔬 Leucine note: white beans are a good plant protein but fall below the 2.5g leucine threshold per portion. The cottage cheese blended into the sauce here closes that gap — it's why this pasta hits ~41g protein and still triggers MPS effectively.
subtitle: White beans · pasta · spinach · garlic-parmesan sauce · ~25 min

steps: Cook basmati rice: rinse rice, simmer in salted water 12–14 min. Fluff and set aside.
Cube paneer into 2cm pieces. Pat dry with paper towel so it browns, not steams.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high. Fry paneer until golden on all sides (~5 min). Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté diced onion 5 min until soft. Add minced garlic and grated ginger — cook 2 min.
Add garam masala and smoked paprika. Stir 1 min to toast the spices.
Add crushed tomatoes. Simmer uncovered 10 min until sauce thickens.
Reduce heat to low heat. Stir in Greek yogurt and cottage cheese gradually to avoid splitting. Season with salt.
Return paneer to the pan. Add spinach and stir until wilted (~2 min).
Portion rice into containers. Top with paneer tikka masala sauce.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Take the pan off the heat before stirring the yogurt and cottage cheese in a spoonful at a time; if the sauce is bubbling, the dairy curdles and the masala turns grainy.
💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge but does not freeze well, as the yogurt sauce splits on thawing. Reheat gently at 50 percent power for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring twice, and stop as soon as it is hot.
subtitle: Paneer · basmati rice · tomato-cream masala · ~35 min

steps: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cube sweet potato into 2cm pieces. Toss with olive oil, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Spread sweet potato on a lined baking tray. Roast 25–30 min, flipping halfway, until caramelised.
Cook brown rice: rinse, simmer in salted water 12–14 min. Fluff and cool.
Drain and rinse black beans and corn. Dice red onion and halve cherry tomatoes.
In a large bowl, combine black beans, corn, cherry tomatoes, red onion, minced garlic, lime juice, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Assemble: divide rice into containers. Top with roasted sweet potato, black bean salsa mix.
Top each bowl with shredded cheddar. Add a dollop of Greek yogurt and cottage cheese to each container when serving.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.

🔬 Leucine note: black beans are leucine-limited as a sole protein source. The Greek yogurt and cottage cheese on top bring each portion above the 2.5g leucine threshold — the point where muscle protein synthesis is maximally activated.
💡 Pack the cheddar, Greek yogurt and cottage cheese separately and add them after reheating; heated yogurt goes thin and watery across the rice.
💡 Reheat the rice and sweet potato at 700 W for about 2 minutes, then spoon the bean salsa over cold; it keeps 4 days, but heating it dulls the raw onion, lime and tomato.
subtitle: Black beans · sweet potato · rice · salsa · ~50 min

steps: Cook brown rice in rice cooker.

Make the mango salsa: dice the mangoes, cucumbers, red onion, and jalapeño. Zest 1 lime and set the zest aside for the fish, then juice 2 of the limes into the salsa with the chopped cilantro, salt, and pepper. Refrigerate.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Season tilapia with cumin, garlic powder, lime zest, salt, and pepper.
Bake tilapia on a lined tray 12–14 min until it flakes easily.
Portion rice and one tilapia fillet into each container. Top with mango salsa.
Cut the remaining lime into 7 wedges and add one to each container to squeeze over at serving.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Tilapia is delicate: store the fillets whole in the container, keep only 3 days and do not freeze once cooked, as thawed cooked fish turns watery and falls apart.
💡 Keep the mango salsa in its own pot and spoon it over cold; reheat only the rice and fish, covered, at 50 percent power for 2 minutes so the fish warms through without going rubbery.
subtitle: Tilapia · jasmine rice · mango salsa · cucumber · lime · ~35 min

steps: Lightly spray a large skillet with oil. Scramble all the eggs until cooked. Set aside.
In the same skillet, cook the beef bacon until crispy. Set aside on paper towels.
Without draining the pan, cook the frozen hashbrowns and diced bell pepper in the same skillet, stirring as they cook.
Once hashbrowns are golden, transfer to a large bowl and weigh. Divide equally and portion into containers.
Distribute scrambled eggs and fresh baby spinach evenly among the containers.
Scatter the fat-free cheddar over the hot hashbrowns and eggs, divided evenly between the containers so it softens as it sits.
Add bacon (a strip or two per container). Top with halved cherry tomatoes.
Optional: serve with sugar-free ketchup.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Divide turkey sausage into equal portions (one per serving) and shape into patties. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Cook patties in a lightly oiled skillet until fully cooked through. Set aside on paper towels.

Cook the eggs to your preferred doneness in the same skillet, pouring 50 g of the liquid egg whites around each one — 150 g across the batch, 1 egg plus 50 g whites per sandwich. Set aside. mist the skillet with cooking spray and toast the bagels face-down until golden.
Assemble: bagel bottom → cheese slice → turkey patty → egg → baby spinach → sliced tomato → bagel top.
Serve immediately or wrap for meal prep.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Grate the carrot finely. Squeeze out excess moisture with a paper towel — this is important.
In a bowl, mix: grated carrot, Greek yogurt, protein powder, egg, oat flour, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt. Mix until thick batter forms.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium, spray with oil.
Scoop batter into the pan to form pancakes. Cook 3–4 min per side until golden and set.
For the chocolate topping: mix Greek yogurt + chocolate protein powder + a little milk until creamy. Pour over the pancakes. (optional — not counted in the macros)
Serve immediately. Optional: drizzle honey or add fresh berries.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Toast the bread slices.
Season cottage cheese with salt, pepper, fresh parsley, and optional chilli flakes.
Spread cottage cheese on toast and serve.
Optional: add sliced tomato or cucumber on top.

😴 Pre-sleep tip: cottage cheese is ~80% casein — the slowest-digesting dairy protein. Eating it before bed sustains muscle protein synthesis overnight for 6–8 hours. This makes it one of the best pre-sleep foods in the library. If you're having it before bed, skip the toast and add a small handful of berries instead to keep carbs minimal.
💡 Season the cottage cheese for the week and keep it in a sealed tub for 4 days; toast and assemble each morning, since dressed toast goes soft within 20 minutes.
💡 Drain any whey off the top of the tub and sit the sliced cucumber and tomato on kitchen paper first, otherwise the toast turns wet before you finish it.
Add rice and water to a rice cooker. Let cook fully.
In a large nonstick skillet, cook the ground beef with diced bell pepper until fully browned. Season with salt and pepper. Remove and set aside.
Using the same skillet, scramble the eggs until fully cooked. Set aside.
Once rice is done, transfer beef, eggs, and rice to a large bowl and mix well.
Weigh total mixture in grams, divide equally into containers.
Top each container with cheddar and mozzarella cheese, halved cherry tomatoes, and fresh baby spinach.
Optional: pack a small portion of sugar-free syrup on the side for a sweet-savoury combo.
🟡 Add 0.5 g turmeric and a pinch of black pepper while cooking — activates curcumin absorption (piperine effect) for anti-inflammatory benefit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Stovetop · batch cook · ~35 min

steps: In a large skillet, spray oil and scramble the eggs with salt and pepper until fully cooked. Set aside.
Using the same skillet, cook the ground beef with diced bell pepper until fully browned. Season with garlic, paprika, onion powder. Set aside.
Cook beef bacon until crispy. Set aside on paper towels.
Lay out tortilla wraps. Add shredded cheese, beef, scrambled eggs, a handful of baby spinach, and a slice of bacon to each wrap.
Drizzle sriracha mayo if desired. Fold ends in, roll tightly. (optional — not counted in the macros)
Toast each burrito on medium-high heat until golden brown on all sides.
Cool completely before refrigerating. Wrap individually in foil for easy grab-and-go.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Wrap · Stovetop · ~35 min

steps: Crack the whole eggs and egg whites into a bowl and whisk.
Lightly spray a non-stick pan with oil and cook over medium heat.
Toast the bread slices.
Serve eggs on toast with fresh baby spinach and halved cherry tomatoes alongside. Optional: add smoked salmon for extra protein.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Spoon of plain 0% Greek yogurt into a bowl.
Top with mixed seeds and berries.
Avoid flavoured yogurts — they add unnecessary sugar. (optional — not counted in the macros)
Optional: add a scoop of unflavoured protein powder for extra protein.
💡 Portion the yogurt into pots for 4 days but add the seeds on the day so they stay crunchy; frozen berries thaw into the yogurt overnight and make a natural swirl.
💡 If adding protein powder, whisk it into a spoonful of yogurt to make a paste first, then fold in the rest; tipping it straight in leaves dry lumps.
Cook the eggs to your preference (scrambled, fried, or boiled).
Slice smoked turkey and arrange alongside the eggs. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Toast the bread slices and serve.
Plate fat-free cottage cheese in a small bowl.
Halve cherry tomatoes for freshness and acidity.
Pull a double espresso and combine with skimmed milk.
Blend the whey protein with the espresso-milk for the protein hit.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.

💪 Bulk note: at 852 kcal and 98g protein, this is designed for aggressive muscle gain phases. If you're on a cut or maintenance, halve the bread and skip the whey — keeps it around 600 kcal with ~75g protein.
Combine rolled oats, milk, Greek yogurt, and whey protein in a jar or bowl. Stir well until evenly mixed.
Top with blueberries, sliced banana, and peanut butter.
Drizzle with maple syrup to taste.
Eat immediately for fresh texture, or refrigerate overnight as overnight oats for a thicker, denser consistency.
💡 Make up to 3 jars ahead; the oats thicken overnight, so loosen with a splash of milk in the morning. Add banana and peanut butter on the day, as the banana browns.
💡 Dissolve the whey in the milk before adding oats and yogurt, otherwise the powder clumps into chalky pockets that you find at the bottom of the jar.
Add Greek yogurt, protein powder, frozen berries, and almond milk to a blender.
Blend on high until thick and smooth — thicker than a drink. Add more milk only if needed.
Pour into a bowl.
Top with mixed seeds, coconut flakes, crushed nuts, or more berries. Serve immediately.
💡 Blend and eat straight away, since the bowl softens to a drink within 15 minutes; if you must make it ahead, freeze the blended base in a pot and stir it after 10 minutes on the bench.
💡 Load the almond milk and yogurt into the blender first, then powder, then frozen berries on top, and pulse rather than run it flat out to keep the mix thick.
Divide ground turkey into equal portions (one per serving). Form each into a thick round patty.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat, spray with oil. Cook turkey patties until fully cooked through. Set aside on paper towels. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.

Cook each egg in the skillet to your preferred doneness (egg molds help keep them round), pouring 50 g of the liquid egg whites around each one — 200 g across the batch, 1 egg plus 50 g whites per sandwich. lightly mist the skillet with cooking spray. Place bagels face-down and toast until golden.
Assemble each sandwich: bottom bagel half → a slice of cheese → a turkey patty → an egg → baby spinach → sliced tomato → top bagel half.
Serve immediately or wrap individually for meal prep. Reheat in microwave 60 sec.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
subtitle: Stovetop · batch cook · ~25 min

steps: In a bowl or jar, combine rolled oats, skimmed milk, Greek yogurt, and whey protein. Stir until fully mixed and smooth.
Fold in blueberries and dust generously with cinnamon.
Eat immediately for fresh texture, or refrigerate 15–30 min for a thicker overnight oats consistency.
💡 Jars keep 3 days in the fridge; the oats absorb the milk overnight, so loosen with a splash of skimmed milk. The chocolate whey and cinnamon deepen after a night chilled.
💡 Stir the whey into the yogurt and milk until glossy before the oats go in; add blueberries last and fold gently so they do not bleed purple through the whole jar.
In a bowl or jar, combine rolled oats, skimmed milk, Greek yogurt, and whey protein. Stir until fully mixed.
Top with sliced banana and blueberries. Dust with cinnamon.
Eat immediately or refrigerate as overnight oats for a denser, colder texture.
💡 Make 3 jars at a time and add the banana on the morning you eat it; sliced banana left in the jar browns and goes slimy by the second day.
💡 If the mixture is stiff after a night in the fridge, add 20 ml skimmed milk rather than water, which thins it without diluting the chocolate whey flavour.
In a bowl or jar, combine rolled oats, skimmed milk, Greek yogurt, and whey protein. Stir well until smooth.
Top with sliced banana.
Melt the dark chocolate in a microwave (30 sec bursts, stirring between). Drizzle over the bowl.
Crumble half a Lotus biscuit on top and finish with a dust of cinnamon. Serve immediately.
💡 Prep the oat base for 3 days but melt the chocolate and add banana and biscuit the morning you eat it; a stored drizzle sets hard and the biscuit goes soft.
💡 Melt the 15 g of dark chocolate in 20-second bursts at 50% power; it looks solid until stirred, and one extra burst at full power seizes it into a grainy lump.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease or line an 8×8 inch (20×20 cm) baking dish with parchment paper.
Mash the ripe bananas thoroughly in a large bowl until smooth. Soak the medjool dates in warm water for 5 minutes, then blend or mash them into a paste.
Whisk the eggs into the mashed banana. add the Greek yogurt and date paste. Stir until combined.
Sift in the cocoa powder, protein powder, almond flour, and baking powder. Fold gently until a smooth batter forms — do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared baking dish and smooth the top. Scatter milk chocolate chips evenly over the surface.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until the centre is just set and a toothpick comes out with moist crumbs (not wet batter).
Remove from the oven and allow to cool completely in the dish before slicing into 9 equal portions.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days, or freeze portions for up to 2 months.
💡 Cool the tray completely, ideally 2 hours or overnight in the fridge, before slicing; warm banana brownies tear, and the squares firm up noticeably once chilled.
💡 Freeze squares on a tray, then bag them for 2 months; thaw in the fridge overnight or microwave from frozen for 20 seconds for a warm, fudgy portion.
Mix Greek yogurt, powdered peanut butter (PB Fit), whey protein powder, and honey in a bowl until smooth.
Spread the mixture evenly over the rice cakes.
Melt dark chocolate chips in a microwave-safe bowl (50% power, 30 sec intervals, stirring between each).
Spread melted chocolate over the rice cakes.
Sprinkle a pinch of sea salt on top.
Place in the freezer for at least 15 minutes to set.
Store in freezer and eat directly from frozen.
💡 These are meant to live in the freezer; keep them in a sealed tub with baking paper between layers and eat straight from frozen, as a thawed rice cake goes soft and chewy within 10 minutes.
💡 Spread the yogurt layer right to the edge and get the melted chocolate over it quickly to seal the surface, or the rice cake underneath draws in moisture and loses its snap.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a loaf tin with parchment paper.
Blend bananas, eggs, and cottage cheese until completely smooth.
Transfer to a bowl. Add oat flour, protein powder, matcha powder, and optional baking powder. Stir until thick and uniform.
Pour into tin. Bake 30 min — toothpick should come out clean.
Make the topping while baking: mix Greek yogurt + matcha powder + protein powder until creamy.
Cool completely before unmoulding. Spread topping over bread.
Top with berries. Slice into portions.
💡 Bake the loaf up to 5 days ahead but store it untopped in the fridge and add the matcha yogurt and berries per slice, since a topped loaf weeps within a day.
💡 Blend the cottage cheese until no curds remain and test the centre with a skewer at 30 minutes; protein powder loaves look done on top while still wet in the middle.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, mix together: Greek yogurt, pumpkin purée, self-rising flour, coconut flour, cocoa powder, protein powder, baking powder, vanilla extract, Truvia brown sugar, and egg.
Add almond milk 15 ml at a time until you reach a cookie dough consistency (not too wet).
Scoop equal portions onto the parchment-lined baking sheet. Flatten slightly.
Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes until set. Remove and allow to cool completely.
Make the frosting: mix a small amount of Greek yogurt with a pinch of vanilla extract until smooth.
Frost cooled cookies. Top with crushed chocolate sandwich cookies if desired.
💡 Unfrosted cookies keep 5 days in the fridge and freeze for 2 months; frost only the ones you plan to eat that day, as the yogurt frosting softens the cookie beneath.
💡 Add the almond milk 15 ml at a time and wait a minute between additions; coconut flour keeps absorbing liquid, so a dough that looks dry often needs less than you think.

steps: Freeze bananas in advance — peel and bag them whole.
Each serving: blend the frozen banana, oats, protein powder, and almond milk.
Blend 45 seconds until smooth. Drink immediately.
Can batch-prep oat+powder portions in zip bags for fast morning assembly.
⏱️ Timing: drink 60–75 min before training for optimal fuel. If training within 30 min, skip the oats and use just banana + protein powder + milk — faster to digest.
💡 Peel and freeze the bananas in halves rather than whole; halves blend without straining the motor, and bagging oats and powder per serving gets you a one-minute morning.
💡 Blend the almond milk with the oats first for 20 seconds, then add banana and powder; this softens the oats so the smoothie is smooth rather than gritty and stays drinkable.

steps: No prep required.
Portion chocolate milk per serving (keep cartons refrigerated).
Pair with a banana and a few rice cakes.
Consume 30–45 min before training.
💡 Decant the chocolate milk into 250 ml bottles for the week and keep the bananas out of the fridge; a cold banana goes grey and mealy while a room-temperature one ripens on schedule.
💡 Have this 30–45 minutes before training as written; if you are prone to a sloshing stomach, halve the milk, keep the rice cakes, and drink the rest after the session.
subtitle: Low-fat chocolate milk · banana · rice cakes · ~10 min

steps: Cook liquid egg whites in a non-stick pan over medium heat, stirring until just set — 2–3 min.
Toast the bread slices.
Spread the low-sugar strawberry jam across the toast — 20 g per serving, 140 g across the batch. Serve the egg whites alongside.
Quick to make fresh each morning — no bulk prep needed.
⏱️ Timing: eat 60–75 min before training. The egg whites digest fast and the toast + jam delivers the carbs you need without the fat that would slow gastric emptying.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.

steps: Portion Greek yogurt per serving into containers.
Add thawed or frozen mixed berries to each.
Top with granola and a drizzle of honey.
Keep granola separate until eating if prepping more than 2 days ahead — prevents sogging.
⏱️ Timing: eat this 60–75 min before training. The carb-protein combo from berries + yogurt + granola gives a steady energy release without GI discomfort mid-session.
💡 Portion the yogurt and frozen berries into tubs for up to 4 days; the berries thaw overnight and bleed a little juice, which is fine, but bag the granola separately so it stays crunchy.
💡 Eat this 60 to 75 minutes before training so the yogurt has time to sit; if your session is closer than that, halve the yogurt and keep the berries and honey for faster carbs.

steps: In each jar or container: combine rolled oats + a scoop of protein powder + chia seeds.
Pour almond milk over each. Stir well.
Seal and refrigerate overnight (or up to 4 days).
In the morning, top with sliced banana or berries. Eat cold or microwave 60 sec.

⏱️ Timing note: this meal is best consumed 2–3 hours before training. If training within 60 min, swap the fat-containing ingredient for plain Greek yogurt or a banana to avoid slowing gastric emptying and GI discomfort during your workout.
💡 Stir each jar again after 10 minutes so the chia and protein powder hydrate evenly rather than settling into a dense layer at the bottom; the jars keep 4 days chilled.
💡 Add the banana only on the morning you eat it, as sliced banana browns and turns mushy in the fridge, and microwave for 60 seconds at 600 W if you prefer it warm.

Spread peanut butter across the rice cakes.
Slice half a banana over the top.
Drizzle honey. Eat 30–45 min before training.

⏱️ Timing note: this meal is best consumed 2–3 hours before training. If training within 60 min, swap the fat-containing ingredient for plain Greek yogurt or a banana to avoid slowing gastric emptying and GI discomfort during your workout.

steps: Add skimmed milk, oats, dates, and almond butter to a blender.
Add protein powder and a pinch of cinnamon and Himalayan salt.
Blend on high for 60 seconds until completely smooth.
Pour and serve immediately, or refrigerate up to 24 hours.
🍽️ Meal note: at 742 kcal and 69g protein, this shake is a complete meal replacement — count it as your main meal, not a snack. It's ideal for post-workout or busy mornings when you can't cook.
💡 Soak the oats in the milk for 10 minutes before blending so they break down fully instead of leaving a gritty texture; blend the dates first if your blender is a low-powered one.
💡 This shake thickens noticeably after a night in the fridge as the oats swell, so if you batch it, loosen with 50 ml extra milk and shake hard before drinking within 24 hours.
Add milk, banana, and dates to blender first.
Add peanut butter, cocoa powder, protein powder, and a pinch of salt.
Blend 60 seconds until smooth and creamy.
Serve immediately.
💡 Freeze the banana and dates in a bag the night before; frozen fruit gives a thick, cold shake without ice diluting the cocoa and peanut flavour.
💡 Drink this within 60 to 90 minutes after training, or 2 hours before, as 16 g fat from the peanut butter sits heavily if taken right before lifting.
Add water/ice and dates to blender base.
Add banana, pineapple, kale, and spinach.
Add coconut cream, peanut butter, protein powder, and salt. (optional — not counted in the macros)
Blend on high 60–90 seconds until smooth.

💡 Portion the banana, pineapple and greens into freezer bags for up to 3 months; tip a bag into the blender with the coconut milk and protein for a 2-minute breakfast.
Combine coconut water, frozen berries and pineapple in blender.
Add Greek yogurt and protein powder.
Blend 45 seconds until smooth.
Serve immediately.
💡 At under 4 g fat and 30 g protein, this is your fastest-digesting smoothie in the set, so it works as a post-session drink within 30 minutes of finishing.
💡 Blend the frozen berries with only half the coconut water first, then add the rest with the yogurt and whey; a small pour of liquid to start stops the blades spinning freely above the fruit.
Whisk matcha powder with a splash of warm water to dissolve.
Add milk, strawberries, protein powder, and honey to blender.
Add dissolved matcha.
Blend 45 seconds. Serve over ice.
💡 Sift the matcha into warm water, not hot, and whisk to a paste before it meets the milk; dry matcha added straight to the blender clumps and leaves bitter green specks.
💡 Fresh strawberries make this thin, so pour it over ice immediately rather than storing it, as the whey and milk separate into layers within a few hours in the fridge.
Add almond milk, banana, and all powders to blender.
Add a pinch of Himalayan salt.
Blend 45 seconds until smooth.
Serve chilled.
💡 Peanut butter powder and cocoa both clump against the blender wall, so add them on top of the liquid and banana, never first, and scrape down once halfway through.
💡 Pour into an ice-cube tray and freeze for a month; five cubes blended with a splash of almond milk gives a thick shake for after training without any extra prep.
Add light coconut milk, mango, banana, and dates to blender.
Add protein powder and salt.
Blend 60 seconds until silky smooth.
Serve chilled.
💡 With 60 g whey in only 100 ml coconut milk this is very thick, so use frozen mango and banana for texture but add 100 ml cold water if your blender labours.
💡 Shake any leftover well before drinking within 24 hours; the coconut fat rises and sets in a layer at the top when it is chilled.
Add milk, banana, dates, cocoa powder, and protein to blender.
Optional: brew 1–2 espresso shots, let cool slightly, and add to blender for a caffeine boost.
Blend 45 seconds. Serve over ice.

💡 Blend and freeze in a lidded cup the night before a morning session, then let it thaw for 20 minutes; drink it 45 to 60 minutes before training so the caffeine lands during your warm-up.
Add all ingredients to blender.
Blend 60 seconds until deep purple and creamy.
Taste and adjust sweetness with extra dates if needed.
Serve immediately.

💡 Skip the dates at first and taste before adjusting; frozen berry mixes vary in sweetness and the banana alone often carries it, saving 60 kcal a serving.

Top with crumbled feta, chopped basil and mint, and a drizzle of balsamic glaze.

Quick-pickle thinly sliced onions in vinegar and salt.

Taste and adjust sweetness — add another 5 ml maple syrup if needed.
Transfer to a glass container or small dish.

Pour melted chocolate evenly over the mousse.
Refrigerate until the chocolate shell hardens (about 20 min). Crack through and enjoy!

Add drained pasta to a large bowl. Pour over the pesto-cottage cheese sauce and toss, adding pasta water a splash at a time to reach a silky consistency. No oil needed.
Fold in drained sun-dried tomatoes. Taste and adjust salt, lemon, and herbs.
Divide into 4 meal prep containers. Refrigerates 4 days — sauce thickens when cold, add a splash of water when reheating.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Press tofu for at least 20 min to remove excess water (wrap in a clean towel and place something heavy on top). Cut into 2 cm cubes.

Preheat oven to 210°C. Toss tofu cubes with soy sauce and 30 ml teriyaki sauce. Spread on a baking tray lined with baking paper — no oil needed. Bake 25–30 min, flipping halfway, until golden and chewy.
Cook quinoa in 480 mL salted water: bring to boil, cover and simmer 15 min, rest 5 min. Fluff.
Steam the broccoli and bell pepper in a pan with a splash of water for 5 min — no oil. Stir in the 20 g minced garlic for the last minute and season with the remaining soy sauce.
Divide quinoa into 4 containers. Top with tofu, broccoli, bell pepper, and edamame. Drizzle remaining teriyaki sauce over each bowl.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Cook soba noodles per packet instructions (3–4 min). Drain and rinse immediately under cold water — this stops overcooking and keeps them from clumping.
Make peanut sauce: whisk together peanut butter, soy sauce, maple syrup, lime juice, garlic, and 4–75 ml water until smooth. No oil needed — the water thins it perfectly.
In a large bowl, combine cold noodles, shredded cabbage, and thawed edamame.
Pour peanut sauce over and toss well to coat everything evenly.
Divide into 4 containers. Refrigerates 3 days. Top with sesame seeds, sliced chilli, or spring onion before eating.
💡 Add 2.5 g fresh grated ginger (or 1.5 g ground) — reduces post-workout muscle soreness (DOMS) and supports digestion.
Sear the diced chicken in a hot dry non-stick pan until golden and just cooked through, then lift it out. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Crisp the gnocchi in the same pan until golden at the edges, picking up the chicken fond.
Add the garlic and spinach and cook about a minute until the spinach wilts.
Take the pan OFF the heat, then stir in the yogurt, parmesan and herbs. Off the heat is the whole trick — direct heat splits yogurt into a grainy mess.
Return the chicken and toss until everything is coated. Season and serve.
💡 Crisping the gnocchi before saucing gives you chewy golden edges that boiling alone never produces.
Cook the rice per packet instructions and keep it covered.
Toss the diced chicken in the cornstarch until lightly coated, then leave it 5 minutes while you mix the sauce. The rest is what makes the coating crisp properly.
Stir the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar and garlic together in a small bowl.
Sear the chicken in a hot pan with the sesame oil, leaving it undisturbed in places so it turns golden rather than steaming. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Once the chicken is cooked through and crisp, pour in the glaze and toss about a minute until sticky and coating every piece.
Serve over the rice, finished with spring onion and sesame seeds.
💡 Add the glaze only at the end. The sugar in it burns fast — you want it sticky, not scorched.
Cook the rice per packet instructions and keep it covered.

Mix the ground chicken with the garlic, ginger, egg white and panko, then roll into small meatballs with damp hands. Don't overwork it — handling makes them dense instead of tender. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Brown the meatballs on all sides in a hot dry non-stick pan, then lift them out. They finish cooking in the sauce.
Add the curry paste to the same pan and fry 1 minute until fragrant, scraping up the browned bits. Blooming the paste in heat is what wakes up the flavour.
Pour in the coconut milk, broth and fish sauce, stir, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Return the meatballs and simmer 8–10 min until cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Finish with the lime juice and serve over the rice.
💡 Meatballs and sauce keep 4 days chilled or 3 months frozen; reheat gently in a covered pan with a splash of water rather than the microwave, which tightens the ground chicken.
💡 Store the jasmine rice in its own tub and reheat it separately with a wet paper towel over it; rice left sitting in coconut curry overnight absorbs the sauce and turns gluey.
Toss the cubed chicken thigh with the shawarma spice, half the lemon juice, the olive oil and a generous pinch of salt. Leave at least 15 min so the seasoning penetrates.
Grate the garlic straight into the yogurt, add the remaining lemon juice and half the parsley, and stir until creamy.

Get a skillet properly hot before the chicken goes in. Cook in a single layer until deeply browned at the edges and cooked through — crowding the pan steams it grey. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Combine the tomato, cucumber, red onion and remaining parsley just before serving so it stays crisp.
Warm the flatbread briefly in a dry skillet, spread the garlic yogurt down the centre, add chicken and salad, and roll tightly.
💡 Thigh over breast here — it stays juicy under the hard char that shawarma needs.
Boil the lasagne sheets until just pliable, then drain and lay them flat so they don't stick together.
Wilt the spinach, cool it, then squeeze out as much water as you can. Wet spinach makes a watery filling.
Combine the chopped chicken, ricotta, spinach, egg white, parmesan, garlic and herbs until evenly mixed. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Spread the filling thinly over each sheet and roll each one up without squeezing the filling out the ends.
Spread a layer of passata across a baking dish, sit the rolls on top seam-side down, then spoon over the rest.
Scatter the mozzarella over the top and bake at 190°C for 20–25 min until bubbling and browned in patches.
Rest 5 minutes before serving, then scatter with parsley.
💡 Keep the cheese on top rather than layered through — you get the browned crust without tripling the fat.
Cook the onion low and slow in the olive oil, 15–20 min, until deeply golden, soft and jammy. Rushing this on high heat gives you burnt edges and raw centres, not sweetness.
Stir the yogurt with the horseradish, dijon and lemon juice until smooth.
Season the sirloin and sear in a hot skillet to medium-rare, then rest it before slicing against the grain.
Spread the sauce over the bread, then layer the steak, caramelised onions, gruyère and rocket.
Toast the closed sandwich in a dry skillet, pressing gently, until the bread is crisp and the cheese has just melted.
Rest a minute before cutting so the juices stay in the sandwich rather than on the board.
💡 Caramelise a full batch of onions at once, 5 or 6 onions on low for 40 minutes, and portion them into 75 g pots; they keep a week chilled or freeze for 3 months.
💡 Store the seared, sliced steak separately for up to 3 days and build the sandwich fresh; toast it in a dry pan under a weight, as a pre-assembled one goes limp from the horseradish yogurt.
Cook the pasta to al dente, reserving a splash of the cooking water before draining.
Toss the chicken with the cajun seasoning and black pepper, then sear in the olive oil until browned at the edges and cooked through. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Add the pepper and garlic, cooking briefly until tender but still slightly crisp.
Lower the heat, stir in the evaporated milk and cream cheese, and let the sauce turn smooth.
Fold in the pasta and chicken, tossing until coated, loosening with pasta water if needed.
