Scatter with parsley and plenty of black pepper.
💡 Evaporated milk gives you a cream-textured sauce for a fraction of the fat — it thickens because it's already concentrated, not because of added fat.
Cook the rice per packet instructions and keep it covered.
Pat the salmon completely dry and season with the garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Sear presentation-side down in the olive oil until deeply golden, then lift it out — it will finish in the sauce.
Soften the garlic and sun-dried tomatoes in the same pan, then add the evaporated milk and reduce gently until it coats a spoon.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, then take the pan OFF the heat before stirring in the yogurt and lemon juice. Off the heat keeps it silky instead of grainy.
Return the salmon to warm through, then plate over the rice and finish with basil and cracked pepper.
💡 Keep the sauce and salmon together for 2 days at most, and reheat in a covered pan on low with a spoon of water; the microwave overcooks the fish and splits the yogurt.
💡 If the evaporated milk sauce reduces too far it turns sticky, so pull it while it still runs off the spoon; it thickens again once the spinach and yogurt go in.
Toss the sweet potato and cauliflower with the olive oil, cumin and paprika and roast at 200°C until soft and caramelised, holding a few pieces back for the topping.
Soften the onion in a pot over medium heat until translucent.
Poach the chicken breast in the broth until cooked through, then lift out, shred, and set aside to stir back in at the end. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Add the roasted veg, the cannellini beans and the broth, and simmer 5 minutes to bring it together.
Blend until completely smooth, adding a splash more broth if it is too thick. Blend a minute longer than feels necessary — that is the difference between grainy and silky.
Ladle into bowls and finish with the reserved roasted veg and parsley.
💡 The chicken and cannellini beans together are what make this a meal rather than a starter — the beans bring the fibre, the chicken brings the protein.
Boil the rigatoni until just al dente, reserving a little pasta water before draining.

Blitz the cottage cheese, milk, garlic, parmesan and lemon juice until completely smooth and free of curds. Blending is not optional — unblended cottage cheese stays lumpy no matter how long you warm it.
Season the steak and cook in a lightly oiled hot skillet until browned outside and pink inside. Rest, then slice.
Warm the blended alfredo over low heat, stirring in pasta water until it coats a spoon without becoming heavy.
Fold the rigatoni through the sauce until every piece is glossy.
Plate with the sliced steak alongside, finished with parmesan, cracked pepper and the chilli crisp.
💡 Blend the cottage cheese sauce in a batch and keep it 4 days chilled; it thickens in the fridge, so loosen with warm pasta water or milk over low heat and never let it boil.
💡 Undercook the rigatoni by a minute if batching, and store the pasta, sauce and sliced steak in three tubs; combined, the pasta swells and the sauce goes claggy by day two.
Butterfly the chicken into thin cutlets so they cook fast and evenly. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Season with the garlic powder, paprika, salt and pepper, then sear in the olive oil until deeply golden. Remove and set aside.
Cook the onion and mushrooms in the same pan until browned and their water has cooked off.
Whisk the cornstarch into the COLD broth before it goes near the pan — adding dry starch to hot liquid gives you lumps every time.
Pour into the pan with the thyme and simmer until thick, then return the chicken and coat in the gravy.
Boil the potatoes until tender, then mash with the Greek yogurt and butter.
Char the green beans in a hot dry skillet, then plate everything with extra gravy spooned over.
💡 The gravy-coated chicken keeps 4 days chilled and freezes well, but the mash goes gluey in the microwave; reheat it in a pan with a splash of milk, and keep the beans separate to re-char.
💡 Cook the mushrooms until their liquid has fully evaporated and they are browned, not grey; wet mushrooms water down the gravy and it will never thicken properly, whatever the cornstarch does.
Toss the potato cubes with the olive oil, paprika, salt and pepper.
Air-fry at 200°C for 18 min, shaking the basket halfway, until properly crisp. In an oven, roast 20–25 min at 200°C in a single layer and flip once.
While the potatoes cook, brown the turkey in a pan over medium-high heat with the cumin and garlic powder, 6–8 min. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Scramble the eggs low and slow with a splash of milk — creamy beats rubbery, and low heat is the only way to get there.
Build the box: potatoes, turkey, eggs, then the reduced-fat cheddar scattered over while everything is still hot.
Keep the salsa in a separate container so the potatoes don't go soggy.
💡 Reheat the potatoes in an air fryer rather than a microwave — a microwave turns the crisp edges to steam.
Heat the oven to 180°C and line a baking dish with parchment.
Whisk the whole eggs and egg whites with the garlic powder, paprika, salt and pepper.
Stir in the chicken, spinach, pepper and onion until evenly distributed — mix properly or the filling all sinks to one end. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Pour into the dish and spread level, then scatter the reduced-fat cheddar over the top.
Bake 30–35 min until a knife in the centre comes out clean.
Cool 10 min before slicing — cutting hot gives you a crumbling mess.
💡 Scales cleanly for the week: set the batch size and the shopping list multiplies the tray for you. Keeps 5 days refrigerated and freezes well.
Halve the banana lengthways — flat pieces give you a stable base to layer everything onto.
Freeze the banana for 10 minutes before dipping. A cold base sets the chocolate faster and far more neatly.
Spread the peanut butter over the cut side. This is the caramel layer that makes it taste like the candy bar.
Press the chopped peanuts into the peanut butter so they don't roll off when you dip.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil and drizzle over — the oil helps it set into a clean, snappy shell.
Add a pinch of flaky salt right after the chocolate, before the shell hardens.
Freeze on parchment at least an hour until firm.
💡 Keep the bars frozen in a sealed tub with baking paper between layers for up to a month; eat within 3 minutes of taking one out, as the banana turns mushy once it thaws.
💡 Let the melted chocolate cool for 2 minutes before drizzling; poured straight from the microwave it melts the peanut butter layer and slides off the frozen banana instead of setting.
Slice the chicken breast into two thin cutlets so it cooks through before the crust burns.
Set up two bowls: beaten egg in one; panko, grated parmesan, paprika and garlic powder in the other.
Dip each cutlet in egg, then press firmly into the crumb. Press — don't dust. Loose crumb falls off in the air fryer.
Spray lightly and air-fry at 200°C for 10–12 min, turning once, until golden and 74°C inside. Cool before slicing so the crust stays on.
Toast the sourdough cubes in the air fryer for the last 3–4 min for croutons.
Whisk the yogurt, lemon, Dijon, Worcestershire and garlic with a pinch of salt and pepper. Thin with 5 ml of water if it won't pour.
Box the romaine, cucumber and tomatoes; add the sliced chicken on top; shaved parmesan over.
💡 Keep the dressing and croutons in separate pots. Dress a Caesar the night before and you have soup by lunch.
💡 The post said 43 g protein. 170 g of breast alone is 38 g — with the parmesan and yogurt it is 54. Trust the weights, not the caption.
Heat the oil in a wide pan with a lid. Sweat the onion, carrot and celery with a pinch of salt for 3 min until the onion turns translucent, then add the garlic.
Add the chorizo and cook 2 min until the fat starts to run orange. That fat is the seasoning for the whole pot — no need for more oil.
Add the diced chicken and turn it in the chorizo fat until sealed on the outside, about 2 min. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Stir in the smoked paprika, pepper and the rice; toast the rice for 1 min, unrinsed, so it keeps its starch.
Pour in the stock, scrape the base, bring to a simmer, cover, and leave on the lowest heat for 15 min. Do not stir — that is what makes a risotto gluey.
Check the rice; if still firm, lid back on for 5 min. Then turn the heat up, add the spinach, lid on 60 s, stir through and cook 1 min more.
Taste for salt (the chorizo and stock carry plenty) and box.
💡 As posted this was two chorizo and no chicken: 44 g fat and 26 g protein a serving. One chorizo for flavour, chicken for the protein, and it becomes a real meal-prep main.
💡 Reheat with a splash of water; the rice tightens in the fridge.
Cook the brown rice and let it steam dry with the lid off.
Mix the turkey with the panko, garlic, parsley, oregano, cumin, 3 g salt and plenty of pepper. Work it just until it holds — overworking makes meatballs bouncy.
Roll into 5–6 balls per serving with wet hands, brush with the oil, and bake at 200°C for 18–20 min until 74°C inside and browned on top.
Grate the cucumber, salt it, and squeeze it dry in your fist — this is the whole difference between tzatziki and yogurt soup. Stir into the yogurt with the dill and lemon.
Rice in the box, meatballs on top, tomatoes alongside.
💡 Tzatziki in its own pot; the meatballs reheat, it doesn't.
💡 The book's version was 113 g of turkey and 'a side of veg or rice'. 150 g and the rice built in makes it a complete 42 g-protein main.
Chop the potatoes, toss with half the oil and seasoning, air-fry or roast at 200°C ~25 min.
Season and cook the chicken with the remaining oil, steam the broccoli, finish with lemon. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled; the potatoes freeze poorly, so freeze only the chicken. Reheat potatoes in the air fryer at 200°C for 5 minutes to re-crisp, and microwave the chicken and broccoli separately.
💡 Rinse the chopped potatoes and dry them thoroughly before oiling; surface starch and moisture steam rather than crisp. Cook the chicken to 74°C at the thickest point and rest it 5 minutes.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, and honey in a small bowl.
Heat olive oil in a skillet; cook chicken until browned, 5–6 minutes. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Add broccoli and carrots, cooking for another 3–4 minutes.
Pour in the peanut sauce and toss to coat.
Serve over brown rice with lime wedges.
💡 Refrigerate for 4 days or freeze chicken and rice for 3 months; keep the peanut sauce in a separate pot. Reheat at 700 W with a splash of water, stirring halfway.
💡 Take the pan off the heat before pouring in the peanut sauce; boiling it hard makes the peanut butter seize and turn grainy. Loosen with 15 ml of warm water if it thickens.
Rub chicken with turmeric, cumin, and salt.
Sear chicken in coconut oil until golden, 5 minutes per side. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Add rice, coconut milk, and water; simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Serve once rice is fluffy and chicken is tender.
💡 Cool within an hour and refrigerate for up to 3 days; cooked rice should never sit out. Freezes well for 2 months. Reheat until piping hot, adding 15 ml of water to revive the coconut rice.
💡 Rinse the basmati until the water runs clear before adding it to the pan, and keep the lid on for the full 15 minutes; peeking lets the steam escape and leaves the rice gluey.
In a small bowl, mix Greek yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper to make a light Caesar dressing.
Toss lettuce and chicken with the dressing. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Spoon mixture onto the tortilla, sprinkle with Parmesan, and roll tightly.
Slice in half and serve fresh or chilled.
💡 Store the dressed chicken and lettuce mixture in a container for up to 3 days and roll it into the tortilla on the morning you eat it. Assembled wraps go soggy overnight and do not freeze.

💡 Pat the cooked chicken and washed lettuce dry before tossing with the yoghurt dressing; excess water thins the dressing and soaks through the tortilla. Warm the tortilla for 10 seconds so it rolls without cracking.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Mix olive oil, balsamic vinegar, and honey in a bowl.
Place chicken and veggies on a baking tray, drizzle with glaze, and season with salt and pepper.
Roast for 25 minutes, flipping halfway through until chicken is cooked and vegetables are tender. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled or 3 months frozen. The zucchini softens on reheating, so use an air fryer at 180°C for 6 minutes rather than the microwave to keep the peppers and onion from going limp.
💡 Cut the zucchini and peppers into chunks at least 3 cm wide so they finish at the same time as the chicken, and keep the honey glaze thin to prevent it scorching before the breast reaches 74°C.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Whisk olive oil, balsamic vinegar, honey, and garlic.
Toss chicken and sweet potatoes in the mixture and roast for 25 minutes. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Add green beans and cook another 5 minutes until tender.
Serve drizzled with pan juices.
💡 Refrigerate for 4 days; the sweet potato and chicken freeze well for 2 months but add fresh green beans on reheating. Reheat at 800 W for 2–3 minutes, spooning the pan juices over the top.
💡 Cube the sweet potatoes to 2 cm so they cook through in 25 minutes alongside the breast; larger pieces leave the chicken overcooked. Add the green beans only for the final 5 minutes.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss chicken and Brussels sprouts in olive oil, garlic, and Italian seasoning.
Spread on a baking tray and roast for 25–30 minutes until the chicken is crisp and sprouts are golden. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Serve hot with a drizzle of lemon juice.
💡 Keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes for up to 3 months. Reheat in an air fryer at 190°C for 5 minutes to keep the thigh skin crisp; microwaving softens both chicken and sprouts.
💡 Halve the sprouts and place them cut side down on the tray with room to spare; crowding steams them and leaves them sulphurous. Thighs are forgiving, so take them to 80°C.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over 190°C.
Season chicken with salt, pepper, and basil. Sear 4–5 minutes per side until golden. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Add garlic, tomatoes, and olives; sauté for another 3 minutes.
Toss in spinach until just wilted, then remove from heat and serve warm.

💡 Good for 4 days in the fridge; freezing is fine for the chicken, but leave the spinach out until reheating. Warm through on the hob over medium heat for 3 minutes with the lid on to avoid drying the breast.

💡 Get the pan properly hot before adding the chicken and do not move it for the first 4 minutes; a pale, stuck-on crust means the oil was not hot enough. Add spinach only after the pan is off the heat.
Preheat oven to 190°C.
Mix miso paste, soy sauce, honey, and ginger into a glaze.
Brush over salmon fillets and bake for 15–18 minutes.
Serve with brown rice and green beans, drizzling leftover sauce on top.
💡 Keeps 3 days chilled; cooked salmon freezes for 1 month but dries on thawing. Reheat gently at 500 W for 90 seconds, covered, and keep the leftover glaze in a separate pot to add afterwards.

💡 Blend the miso paste with the honey and soy until smooth before brushing, and bake skin-side down; the sugars in the glaze burn easily, so pull the fillet at 50°C internal for flaky, not chalky, flesh.
Preheat your grill or grill pan to medium-high.
In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, zest, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Brush salmon fillets generously with the mixture and let marinate for 10 minutes.
Grill salmon for 4–5 minutes on each side until flaky and lightly charred.
Serve over warm quinoa with steamed greens and drizzle any leftover dressing on top.

💡 Refrigerate for 3 days and reheat the salmon at 50% microwave power for 2 minutes to stop it overcooking. The quinoa freezes in portions; grilled salmon is best eaten chilled, flaked into the quinoa.
💡 Limit the lemon marinade to 10 minutes; the acid begins to cure the salmon and turns the surface mushy. Oil the grill bars and leave the fillet alone until it releases cleanly.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Mix mustard, honey, and olive oil in a bowl.
Brush over salmon fillets and bake for 12–15 minutes.
Serve with steamed broccoli and spinach drizzled with lemon juice.
💡 Holds 3 days in the fridge; not ideal for freezing once glazed. Reheat at 600 W for 60–80 seconds and steam fresh broccoli and spinach on the day, as reheated greens turn khaki and limp.

💡 Bake the fillet on parchment with the glaze brushed on thickly at the start; pull it at 12 minutes when the centre is still slightly translucent, since the honey glaze overcooks quicker than plain salmon.
Preheat oven to 190°C.
Place cod on parchment-lined baking sheet; drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with dill, salt, and pepper.
Layer lemon slices on top and bake for 15–18 minutes.
Toss green beans with a touch of olive oil and garlic, then roast beside the fish for the last 10 minutes.
💡 Refrigerate for 2 days only; cod flakes fall apart in the freezer once cooked. Reheat covered at 500 W for 90 seconds and add the green beans afterwards so they keep some bite.
💡 Pat the cod dry and season it 10 minutes before baking to firm the flesh; a wet fillet steams in its own liquid and disintegrates. Remove the lemon slices before storing, or the flesh turns bitter.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place tilapia and asparagus on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Drizzle with olive oil, lemon juice, zest, garlic, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Roast for 12–15 minutes until the fish flakes easily and the asparagus is tender-crisp.
Serve warm with a side of lemon slices.
💡 Keeps 2 days chilled; tilapia does not freeze well once cooked. Reheat at 500 W for 60–90 seconds under a damp paper towel and keep the asparagus in a separate pot.
💡 Snap the woody ends off the asparagus and lay spears in a single layer; thin tilapia fillets overcook in a heartbeat, so check at 12 minutes and stop when the flesh just turns opaque.
In a small bowl, mix Greek yogurt, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper to create a creamy sauce.
In another bowl, combine shredded chicken, cucumber, and tomatoes. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Warm the pita breads slightly, then slice open and fill with the chicken mixture.
Spoon the yogurt sauce into each pocket and serve immediately.
💡 Store the chicken, cucumber and tomato filling and the yoghurt sauce in separate pots for up to 3 days; fill the pita when eating so it does not go wet. Pitas freeze well on their own.
💡 Salt the diced cucumber and drain it for 10 minutes before combining; watery cucumber turns the yoghurt sauce thin and floods the pocket. Warm the pita in a dry pan so it opens without tearing.
Melt butter in a skillet and sauté garlic.
Add cod and cook 4 minutes per side.
Add spinach and lemon juice; cover until wilted.
Serve warm.
💡 Eat within 2 days of cooking and skip the freezer. Reheat gently on the hob in a covered pan over low heat for 3 minutes rather than the microwave, which turns cod rubbery.
💡 Keep the garlic in the butter over medium heat and add the cod once it is fragrant, not browned; burnt garlic turns the whole pan bitter. Flip the cod only once or it breaks apart.
Cook pasta and drain. Allow to cool slightly.
In a large bowl, combine pasta, chicken, tomatoes, olive oil, lemon juice, and pesto. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Toss gently to coat evenly and chill before serving.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled and is meant to be eaten cold; do not freeze, as the pesto separates and pasta goes chalky. Stir in a squeeze of lemon and 5 ml of oil before serving.
💡 Cook the pasta to firm al dente, drain and toss with the olive oil while still warm so it does not clump; add the pesto and tomatoes only once cooled so the basil keeps its colour.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Mix olive oil, lemon juice, thyme, and garlic powder.
Brush over cod and bake 12–15 minutes.
Serve with steamed greens.
💡 Refrigerate for 2 days; freezing cooked cod ruins its texture. Reheat at 500 W for 90 seconds under a lid, or eat it cold flaked over greens as a dressed salad.
💡 Brush the lemon oil on just before the cod goes in the oven; acid left to sit turns the surface opaque and mealy. Bake until an inserted knife feels warm and the flakes separate easily.
Add the almond milk to the blender first.
Add the protein powder on top to help it dissolve smoothly.
Add the banana, mint leaves, and ice.
Blend on high for 60 seconds until the mixture becomes creamy, airy, and speckled with mint.
Taste and add an extra mint leaf if you prefer a bolder freshness.
💡 Blend and drink within 30 minutes; the mint oxidises and the shake separates when stored. Freeze peeled banana in 60 g portions so each shake is measured and ready to go.

💡 Pour the almond milk first, then the whey, then the frozen banana and ice on top; this pulls the powder down into the blades rather than caking on the lid. Drink it within an hour of finishing training.
Preheat oven to 190°C.
Combine all ingredients in a bowl; form small balls.
Arrange on a parchment-lined tray.
Bake 20–25 minutes or until golden. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled and freezes for 3 months in a single layer before bagging. Reheat from frozen at 180°C in the air fryer for 8 minutes, or microwave at 700 W with a spoonful of water.
💡 Grate the zucchini, salt it and squeeze it in a tea towel until nearly dry; unsqueezed zucchini releases water in the oven and the meatballs collapse and steam rather than brown.
Spoon Greek yogurt into a bowl.
Add mixed berries and drizzle honey over top.
Sprinkle walnuts for crunch.
Enjoy immediately as a quick and nourishing breakfast.
💡 Portion the yoghurt into containers for up to 4 days, but keep the walnuts in a separate pot or they go soft. Berries can be added frozen the night before; they thaw by morning.
💡 Toast the chopped walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes and cool before sprinkling; raw walnuts taste bitter against the honey. Drain any liquid from thawed berries so the yoghurt stays thick.
Mix all ingredients in a microwave-safe mug until smooth.
Microwave for 60–75 seconds until set but still moist.
Let cool slightly before enjoying with a spoon.
💡 Best eaten straight away; a cake with 30 g of protein powder turns rubbery on reheating. Mix the dry ingredients into several mugs in advance and add banana and milk when ready.
💡 Microwave in 15-second bursts after the first 60 seconds and stop when the top is just set; even 20 seconds too long turns whey-based cakes into a spongy puck.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
In a skillet, heat olive oil and sauté garlic and chili flakes.
Add shrimp and cook until pink, 2–3 minutes per side.
Toss in pasta, lemon juice, and parsley. Mix well and serve.
💡 Lasts 3 days refrigerated; do not freeze once combined, as shrimp turn rubbery. Reheat on the hob with a splash of water and the lid on for 2 minutes, adding the parsley fresh.
💡 Save a ladle of pasta water and add it when tossing so the oil and lemon cling instead of pooling; take the shrimp off the heat the moment they curl into a C shape.
Whisk eggs and egg whites in a bowl until light and fluffy.
Heat olive oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat.
Add bell peppers, spinach, and tomatoes; sauté for 3–4 minutes until softened.
Pour in the eggs and cook gently, stirring occasionally until just set.
Sprinkle cheese over the top and fold gently.
Serve warm with whole-grain toast if desired.
💡 Refrigerate for up to 3 days; freezes for 1 month but the tomatoes turn watery. Reheat at 50% power for 60–90 seconds, stirring once; full power turns scrambled egg rubbery and weeping.
💡 Cook the peppers and tomatoes until their liquid has evaporated before adding the eggs, then keep the heat low and pull the pan off while the curds still look wet; they finish cooking off the heat.
In a mixing bowl, toss cooked quinoa with spinach and roasted red peppers.
Add the grilled chicken slices on top. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Drizzle olive oil and balsamic vinegar, and season with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle pumpkin seeds over the top for crunch and healthy fats.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled and is best eaten cold. Freeze the chicken and quinoa in portions if needed, but pack the pumpkin seeds and balsamic dressing separately to keep them crunchy and bright.
💡 Cool the quinoa spread out on a tray before tossing; warm quinoa wilts the spinach and clumps. Slice the chicken across the grain after resting 5 minutes so the salad is not dry.
Heat olive oil in a skillet. Add turkey, paprika, and garlic powder; cook until browned. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Stir in soy sauce, then remove from heat.
Spoon turkey mixture into lettuce cups.
Wrap and enjoy warm for a flavorful, low-carb lunch.
💡 Store the turkey mince chilled for 4 days or frozen for 3 months; reheat at 700 W for 2 minutes. Keep the lettuce leaves whole and dry in a separate bag and fill them just before eating.
💡 Break the turkey up into a hot pan and let it sit for 2 minutes before stirring so it browns rather than boils in its own juices; add the soy sauce off the heat to avoid a salty scorch.
Spread pesto on one slice of bread.
Layer mozzarella and tomato slices, then drizzle with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Top with the second slice of bread and grill on a pan for 2–3 minutes per side until golden and melty.
Slice diagonally and enjoy warm.

💡 Assemble and grill the same day; a sandwich with 240 g of tomato goes soggy within hours. Prep the mozzarella and tomato slices separately for up to 3 days and reheat in a dry pan, not the microwave.

💡 Salt the tomato slices and rest them on paper towel for 10 minutes to draw out water, and pat the mozzarella dry; toast over medium heat with a weight on top so the cheese melts before the bread burns.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add garlic and sauté until fragrant.
Add shrimp, season with salt and pepper, and cook for 3–4 minutes until pink.
Add zucchini noodles and toss with lemon juice for 1 minute—just until slightly softened.
Serve immediately for a bright, clean flavor.

💡 Store the shrimp and raw zoodles in separate pots for up to 2 days; cooked zucchini noodles turn to water overnight. Warm the shrimp for 1 minute in a pan and toss the zoodles through for 30 seconds.
💡 Salt the spiralised zucchini and drain it on a towel for 15 minutes before cooking, then toss it through for one minute only; any longer and the noodles weep and the shrimp overcook.
Heat olive oil in a skillet. Add onion and garlic, sauté until soft.
Add turkey and cook until browned. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Stir in zucchini and spices; cook another 5–6 minutes until tender.
Serve hot, optionally over rice or greens.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled and freezes for 3 months in portions. Reheat at 800 W for 2–3 minutes, stirring halfway; the zucchini softens further, so undercook it slightly if batch prepping.
💡 Cook the onion until translucent, then push it aside and brown the turkey in a single layer without stirring; add the paprika and cumin with the zucchini so the spices bloom without burning.
In a large bowl, combine greens, orange segments, shrimp, and avocado.
Whisk together olive oil, lime juice, salt, and pepper for dressing.
Drizzle over salad and toss gently before serving.
💡 Keep the cooked shrimp, greens, orange and dressing in separate pots for up to 2 days and assemble on the day; dressed greens wilt within an hour. Add the avocado last.
💡 Cook the shrimp for 2 minutes per side until opaque and chill them fully before adding; warm shrimp wilt the greens. Squeeze lime over the avocado immediately to stop it browning.
Heat sesame oil in a pan, and sauté garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add turkey and cook until browned. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Add broccoli and bell peppers; stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Pour in soy sauce and cook 2 minutes longer before serving.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled and freezes for 3 months, though the broccoli softens on thawing. Reheat in a hot wok for 3 minutes with a splash of water rather than the microwave to keep the peppers crisp.
💡 Have everything cut and the sauce measured before the sesame oil goes in; it burns quickly at high heat, so use it for the garlic and ginger and add a neutral oil for the turkey if the pan smokes.
Mash the avocado with Greek yogurt and lemon juice until smooth.
Stir in the chopped eggs, salt, and pepper.
Spread on tortillas, top with lettuce, and roll up. Slice in half to serve.
💡 The egg salad keeps 2 days chilled with cling film pressed onto the surface to slow browning; assembled wraps do not keep and freezing splits the avocado. Roll on the day you eat it.
💡 Chop the boiled eggs coarsely and fold them in gently so the salad holds texture; over-mashing makes it paste-like. Layer lettuce between the tortilla and filling so the wrap stays dry.
Add yogurt to a bowl and top with peach slices.
Sprinkle chia seeds and walnuts over top.
Drizzle with honey for a soft, floral sweetness.
Enjoy chilled light, fruity, and omega-rich.
💡 Stir the chia seeds into the yoghurt and refrigerate for up to 3 days; they thicken it overnight. Keep the walnuts and honey in a separate pot and slice the peach on the day, as it browns.
💡 Mix the chia seeds through the yoghurt and rest 10 minutes so they hydrate; sprinkled on top they stay gritty. Choose a firm peach and toss the slices in a little lemon juice to stop browning.
In a salad bowl, combine greens, apple, and walnuts.
Add the sliced chicken breast on top. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
In a small bowl, whisk olive oil, vinegar, and honey.
Drizzle dressing over the salad just before serving.
💡 Cook and slice the chicken up to 4 days ahead and keep it chilled with the greens and walnuts; toss the apple in the vinegar dressing separately so it stays pale, and do not freeze.
💡 Rest the chicken for 5 minutes before slicing across the grain so the juices settle; cut it warm and it bleeds moisture into the greens and turns dry.
In a bowl, mix yogurt, lemon zest, and poppy seeds.
Drizzle in honey and stir gently.
Top with berries and almonds for crunch and freshness.
Enjoy chilled the tang of lemon and creaminess of yogurt awaken your senses.
💡 The yogurt, zest and poppy seed base keeps 3 days in a sealed tub; add the berries and almonds when serving, as almonds soften and berries weep overnight. Not one for the freezer.
💡 Zest only the yellow skin of the lemon with a fine grater; the white pith underneath turns the whole bowl bitter, and 5 g is roughly one small lemon's worth.
Heat sesame oil in a pan and cook garlic and chicken until browned. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Add soy sauce, honey, and bell peppers. Sauté for 3–4 minutes until fragrant.
Spoon mixture into lettuce leaves and roll up like small wraps.
💡 The cooked chicken filling keeps 3 days chilled and freezes for 2 months; reheat in a pan or at 700 W for 90 seconds, and store the lettuce leaves dry in a separate tub.
💡 Spread the ground chicken thinly and leave it alone for 2 minutes before breaking it up so it browns rather than steams; add the honey last or it catches and burns.
Pour the almond milk into the blender first to create a smooth base.
Add strawberries, Greek yogurt, and almond butter.
Top with ice for extra thickness and chill.
Blend on medium speed for 20–30 seconds to break down the fruit, then increase to high and blend until creamy and rosy in color.
Scrape down the sides if the almond butter sticks, then blend again for a uniform texture.
💡 Freeze the strawberries, almond butter and yogurt together in a portion bag, then tip into the blender with the milk and whey; the frozen fruit replaces the ice.
💡 Drink it within 30 to 60 minutes of finishing your session and blend the whey into the milk before adding fruit, as almond butter coats dry powder and leaves lumps.
Heat olive oil in a skillet and add garlic; sauté briefly.
Add shrimp and cook until pink (about 3 minutes per side).
Toss in snap peas and zucchini, and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add soy sauce and lemon juice; serve over rice.
💡 Portion the rice and the shrimp stir-fry in the same box and keep for 2 days only, as cooked shrimp deteriorates quickly; microwave at 600 W with a splash of water, not the air fryer.
💡 Pat the shrimp completely dry and add them to a hot pan in one layer; 2 minutes per side is enough, and they should curl into a loose C rather than a tight O, which signals overcooking.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over 175°C and sauté mushrooms until tender (about 5 minutes).
Beat eggs and season lightly.
Pour into skillet, stirring gently until softly set.
Add goat cheese and fold until slightly melted.
Garnish with chives and serve warm.
💡 Eat this fresh where possible; if batching, undercook the eggs slightly, chill for 2 days maximum and reheat covered at 500 W in 30-second bursts. Scrambled egg does not freeze well.
💡 Sauté the mushrooms until their liquid has evaporated before the eggs go in, otherwise it pools and makes the scramble watery; pull the pan off the heat while the curds still look glossy.
In a mixing bowl, whisk together almond milk, chia seeds, and vanilla extract. Stir for about 30 seconds to evenly distribute the chia seeds.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours (or overnight) until the mixture becomes thick and pudding-like.
Once set, stir the chia pudding well to break up any clumps.
In serving glasses, layer chia pudding, Greek yogurt, and sliced strawberries.
Drizzle each parfait with honey and serve chilled for a refreshing, protein-rich start to your morning.
💡 Make the chia pudding in a batch and keep it 5 days chilled; layer with yogurt and strawberries the night before at most, as cut strawberries soften. It is a no-freeze recipe.
💡 Stir the chia and almond milk again after 10 minutes in the fridge; that second stir breaks up the seeds that have sunk and clumped, which is why puddings set unevenly.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over 175°C.
Add diced tomato and cook for 2 minutes.
Beat eggs and pour into the pan, stirring gently.
When nearly set, sprinkle basil and remove from heat.
Serve warm with whole-grain toast if desired.
💡 Best made fresh, but the scramble holds 2 days chilled; reheat gently at 500 W and stop while still slightly wet. Keep extra basil aside and add it fresh at serving.

💡 Cook the diced tomato until its juices have mostly cooked off before adding the eggs; wet tomato loosens the curds and leaves a puddle in the pan. Fold gently with a spatula rather than stirring constantly.
Heat butter in a skillet over medium heat. Add garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add shrimp and cook for 2–3 minutes per side until pink and opaque.
Stir in lemon juice, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper.
Add zucchini noodles, tossing gently for 1–2 minutes until lightly softened.
Serve warm with extra lemon juice if desired.
💡 Keep the shrimp and the raw spiralised courgette in separate containers for up to 2 days, then combine in a hot pan for 90 seconds; reheated courgette noodles collapse into water.
💡 Salt the courgette noodles and let them drain in a colander for 10 minutes, then pat dry; skipping this leaves a watery garlic butter that slides off rather than clinging.
In a saucepan, cook oats in vegetable broth over medium heat until creamy, about 10 minutes.
Stir in chopped spinach and cook another minute until wilted.
Spoon oatmeal into bowls and top with poached eggs and Parmesan.
Crack open the yolk and swirl warm, savory, and perfectly nourishing.
💡 The savoury oats keep 4 days chilled and freeze well in single portions; loosen with 30 ml of broth when reheating on the hob. Poach the eggs fresh each morning, they take 3 minutes.
💡 Add the eggs to barely simmering water with a splash of vinegar and crack each into a small cup first; a rolling boil shreds the white and leaves a ragged, rubbery egg.
Cook pasta according to package instructions. Drain and set aside.
In a skillet, heat olive oil and sauté garlic and mushrooms until browned.
Add almond milk and simmer 3 minutes. Stir in spinach until wilted.
Toss in pasta and sprinkle with Parmesan if desired.
💡 Store for up to 3 days with a spoonful of the almond milk sauce reserved for reheating; warm at 600 W with a splash of water and stir halfway. Freezing turns the pasta mushy.
💡 Almond milk is thin, so simmer it with the mushrooms until reduced by a third before adding the pasta; cook the pasta a minute short and finish it in the sauce so it absorbs the flavour.
Heat olive oil in a skillet and add chickpeas, cumin, and paprika.
Sauté until slightly crispy (6–8 minutes).
Spread Greek yogurt on tortillas, add lettuce and spiced chickpeas.
Roll tightly and cut in half. Serve warm or chilled.
💡 Keep the spiced chickpeas in one box for 4 days and the yogurt and lettuce in another; assemble on the day. Chickpeas alone freeze well and crisp back up in an air fryer at 180°C.
💡 Dry the chickpeas thoroughly on kitchen paper before they hit the oil, or they steam instead of crisping; warm the tortilla for 20 seconds so it rolls without cracking, then wrap in paper to hold.
Warm the tortilla in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 30 seconds each side.
Spread hummus down the center.
Add scrambled egg, mushrooms, and spinach.
Season lightly, roll up, and slice in half.
A perfect protein-packed handheld breakfast.
💡 Wrap tightly in foil and chill for 2 days; reheat unwrapped in an air fryer at 170°C for 4 minutes so the tortilla crisps, or 600 W in the microwave for a softer result. Not for freezing.
💡 Let the mushrooms and egg cool for a few minutes before assembling, and spread hummus right to the edges as a moisture barrier; hot filling steams the tortilla and it tears when rolled.
Heat olive oil in a pot and sauté carrots and celery for 3–4 minutes.
Add chicken broth, green beans, thyme, salt, and pepper. Bring to a gentle boil.
Stir in the shredded chicken and simmer for 15 minutes until flavors meld. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Serve warm, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
💡 Cool fast, chill for 4 days or freeze in 400 ml portions for 3 months; reheat on the hob to a full simmer. Freeze the broth and vegetables without the chicken and stir it in when reheating.
💡 Keep the soup at a gentle simmer once the chicken goes in; boiling shredded breast for 15 minutes wrings it dry and stringy. Cut carrots and celery the same size so they finish together.
In a bowl, add cottage cheese as the base.
Top with tomatoes, avocado, olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Mix gently before eating for a creamy, tangy blend.
💡 Portion the cottage cheese into jars up to 4 days ahead; halve and cut the avocado on the day you eat it, and toss it in the lemon juice straight away so it stays green. No freezing.
💡 Drain the cottage cheese in a sieve for 10 minutes before building the bowl; the whey it sheds otherwise pools with the tomato juice and turns the dressing thin.
Heat a grill pan and lightly brush with olive oil.
Grill halloumi slices for 2–3 minutes per side until golden.
Grill zucchini and bell peppers until tender.
Toss all with greens and drizzle with balsamic vinegar.
💡 Halloumi turns squeaky and firm once cold, so store it separately for 3 days and flash it in a dry pan or air fryer at 200°C for 3 minutes; keep greens and balsamic apart.
💡 Pat the halloumi slices dry and lay them on a properly hot, barely oiled grill pan without moving them for 2 minutes; a cool pan makes them weep brine and stick instead of colouring.
Toast the bread slice to your preferred crispness.
In a small bowl, mash the avocado with a fork until smooth yet slightly chunky. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Heat a nonstick skillet and fry or poach the egg until the yolk is set to your liking.
Spread the mashed avocado evenly over the warm toast, then place the cooked egg on top.
Add a handful of microgreens and a sprinkle of chili flakes for a gentle kick.
Serve immediately for a warm, nourishing breakfast.
💡 This one is assemble-and-eat; if you must prep, mash the avocado with a little lemon juice, press cling film onto the surface and chill for 1 day. Toast, fry and stack in the morning.
💡 Toast the bread properly dark and let it cool for a minute before spreading the avocado; warm, pale toast absorbs the mash and goes limp under the egg within minutes.
Cook pasta according to package directions; drain.
In a skillet, sauté garlic in olive oil, then add spinach until wilted.
Stir in tuna and Greek yogurt. Add pasta, toss, and season with salt and pepper.
💡 Keeps 3 days chilled and does not freeze, as the yogurt sauce splits on thawing; reheat at 500 W with 15 ml of water, stirring every 45 seconds so the sauce loosens without curdling.
💡 Take the pan off the heat before stirring in the Greek yogurt and tuna; boiling yogurt splits into grainy curds. Drain the tuna well first or the sauce goes watery and grey.
Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl, smoothing it lightly so it forms a soft, creamy base.
Add the fresh strawberry slices on top, letting them fan out naturally for a bright, inviting layer.
Sprinkle the chia seeds evenly over the strawberries, giving a light crunch and a boost of nourishment.
Finish with a gentle drizzle of honey for a naturally sweet, soothing touch in every bite.
💡 Cottage cheese portions keep 4 days in sealed jars, but slice the strawberries no earlier than the night before, as cut berries release juice and stain the cheese pink. Never freeze.
💡 Sprinkle the chia over the strawberries rather than into the cheese; stirred in, the seeds swell and turn the bowl gluey by the time you get to it.
Spoon the cottage cheese into a bowl, creating a smooth, creamy base.
Add the fresh berries on top, then sprinkle the chia seeds evenly over them for a gentle crunch and added nourishment.
Drizzle honey over the mixture to add a touch of natural sweetness.
Stir gently to combine the layers, and enjoy immediately while chilled for a refreshing, protein-packed snack.
💡 Build these in jars up to 3 days ahead using whole blueberries or raspberries, which hold better than cut fruit; keep the honey in a small pot to drizzle at serving time.
💡 Use berries straight from the fridge, and if using frozen mixed berries, thaw them in a sieve first so the juice drains away instead of watering down the cottage cheese.
Toast the bread to your preferred crispness.
In a bowl, mash avocado with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread the creamy avocado mixture over toast.
Slice the soft-boiled egg in half and place on top; sprinkle with chili flakes.
Serve immediately for a fresh, satisfying breakfast.
💡 Soft-boil the eggs in a batch, shell them and keep in cold water in the fridge for 3 days; dip in hot water for 1 minute to warm. Do the avocado and toast fresh.
💡 Lower eggs into boiling water for 6 minutes 30 seconds, then straight into iced water; without the ice bath the yolk keeps cooking and sets firm instead of jammy.
Spoon the Greek yogurt into a glass or bowl, smoothing it into an even layer.
Add the berries on top, spreading them so you get a bit in every bite.
Sprinkle the flaxseed evenly over the berries.
Drizzle the honey across the top, then enjoy immediately while everything is fresh and cool.
💡 Layer in small jars and chill up to 2 days; ground flaxseed goes bitter and soft once wet, so keep it in a twist of paper and sprinkle at the last moment. Not freezer-suitable.
💡 Nonfat Greek yogurt weeps water as it sits, so tip off any liquid from the tub and spoon from the thick centre; press the yogurt layer flat so the honey sits on top rather than sinking.
In two clear glasses, layer yogurt, mango, pineapple, and granola.
Sprinkle chia seeds and shredded coconut over the top.
Chill for 5 minutes for a refreshing, beachy vibe — sweet, tangy, and creamy in every bite.
💡 Fresh pineapple contains an enzyme that breaks yogurt down into a watery layer, so keep the fruit in a separate pot and assemble within a day; add the granola last so it stays crunchy.
💡 Pat the diced mango and pineapple dry on kitchen paper before layering; their juices bleed through the yogurt and blur the stripes. Hold the coconut and chia back until serving.
In a bowl, whisk ricotta, egg, almond milk, honey, lemon zest, and vanilla until smooth.
In another bowl, mix flour and baking powder.
Combine wet and dry ingredients; stir gently.
Heat a lightly greased non-stick skillet to 175°C and pour 60 ml batter per pancake.
Cook each side for 2–3 minutes until golden.
Serve with a drizzle of honey and extra lemon zest for brightness.
💡 Cool the pancakes flat on a rack, stack with baking paper between and keep 3 days chilled or 2 months frozen; reheat in a toaster or air fryer at 170°C for 3 minutes.
💡 Stir the flour in with a few strokes only and let the batter rest for 5 minutes; overmixing works the gluten and makes ricotta pancakes tough rather than soft and pillowy.
Heat olive oil and sauté garlic, turmeric, and curry powder.
Add shrimp and cook 2–3 minutes per side.
Pour in coconut milk; simmer until slightly thickened.
Serve over jasmine rice or quinoa.

💡 Chill for 2 days and reheat gently on the hob until just steaming; a microwave overcooks shrimp before the coconut sauce warms. Store the rice or quinoa in its own container and freeze that instead.
💡 Toast the curry powder in oil for 30 seconds at most, then reduce the coconut milk after the shrimp are cooked; light coconut milk splits if it boils hard, so keep it at a simmer.
In a bowl, stir together the yogurt, honey, and cinnamon until smooth and well combined.
In serving glasses, layer a spoonful of the yogurt mixture, followed by diced apple, granola, and walnuts, spreading each layer evenly.
Repeat the layers until the glasses are filled, finishing with a touch of yogurt and a few walnut pieces on top.
Chill briefly if desired, then serve immediately for a creamy, crunchy, and sweet breakfast or snack.
💡 Dice the apple and toss it in a squeeze of lemon, then keep it in a separate lidded pot; the parfait can be layered 1 day ahead but the granola belongs on top only at serving.
💡 Whisk the cinnamon and honey into the yogurt thoroughly before layering, as cinnamon added dry sits in gritty pockets; cut the apple into even 1 cm dice so it spoons up cleanly.
Spoon the cottage cheese into a small bowl or jar, creating a creamy base.
Add the pineapple pieces on top, layering them evenly for a bright, juicy contrast.
Before eating, stir lightly so the cottage cheese and pineapple combine into a sweet-tangy mix, ready to enjoy immediately.

💡 Portion into 4 jars and keep 4 days; pineapple enzymes soften cottage cheese into a watery mess overnight, so add the fruit each morning or use tinned pineapple, which is heat-treated and safe to layer.
💡 Drain the pineapple in a sieve and press lightly before it goes on top; excess juice sinks through the cottage cheese and makes the bottom of the cup sour and thin.
Toast bread until crisp.
Spread cottage cheese evenly over toast.
Top with strawberry slices, drizzle honey, and sprinkle chia seeds.
A simple yet elegant breakfast — creamy, fruity, and lightly sweet.
💡 Make 4 jars at once; they keep 4 days chilled and freeze for a month if you leave the banana out and mash it in on the day. Thaw overnight in the fridge and stir before eating.

💡 Loosen the peanut butter into the almond milk before adding the oats and chia, or it sits in a solid lump at the bottom; the mashed banana thickens overnight, so add a splash more milk than looks right.
In a pan, heat olive oil and add curry powder for 30 seconds.
Stir in chickpeas and coconut milk; simmer for 5–7 minutes.
Add spinach and cook until wilted.
Serve over warm brown rice for a creamy, aromatic meal.
💡 Box the curried chickpeas with the rice; both keep 4 days chilled and freeze together for 3 months. Reheat at 800 W for 3 minutes with 15 ml of water, stirring halfway.
💡 Bloom the curry powder in the oil for 30 seconds only, stirring constantly; it burns bitter fast. Simmer the coconut milk uncovered so it reduces to a coating sauce rather than staying thin.
Cook pasta according to package instructions.
In a pan, heat olive oil and sauté garlic and tomatoes.
Add spinach and cooked pasta; toss together.
Sprinkle Parmesan before serving.
💡 Chickpea pasta firms up and turns crumbly when cold, so keep 2 days at most and reheat at 600 W with 30 ml of water and a lid; never freeze this one.
💡 Boil chickpea pasta 1 minute less than the packet says and rinse briefly; it goes from firm to mushy quickly and keeps cooking in the hot pan with the tomatoes.
Add the yogurt to a small bowl, then sprinkle in the cinnamon and drizzle the honey over the top.
Gently mix everything together until the yogurt becomes smooth, creamy, and lightly sweetened.
Arrange your fresh apple slices on a plate and serve them alongside the yogurt dip, letting each slice be coated in the sweet, spiced creaminess for a refreshing, energizing snack.
💡 The dip keeps 4 days sealed; give it a stir if any whey rises. Slice apples the same day, or hold them in water with a squeeze of lemon for a few hours.
💡 Use thick strained Greek yogurt and mix the honey in a little at a time; adding it all at once thins the dip so it runs off the apple instead of coating it.
In a bowl, combine the yogurt with the finely chopped cucumber, fresh dill, salt, and pepper, letting the ingredients sit together for a moment so the flavors start to blend.
Drizzle a little olive oil over the top, then stir gently until everything is lightly mixed while still keeping a refreshing texture.
Serve chilled with crisp veggie sticks, or simply enjoy it on its own as a cool, soothing snack.
💡 Cucumber keeps releasing water, so store it chopped in its own pot and fold it into the yogurt the day you eat it; the herbed yogurt base alone keeps 4 days and will not freeze.
💡 Scoop out the watery seeds, then salt the chopped cucumber for 10 minutes and squeeze it in a clean cloth; skipping this leaves a thin, sloppy bowl by lunchtime.
Toast bread until crisp.
Spread cottage cheese evenly over toast.
Top with strawberry slices, drizzle honey, and sprinkle chia seeds.
A simple yet elegant breakfast — creamy, fruity, and lightly sweet.
💡 Not one to box up, as toast goes soggy under cottage cheese within the hour. Pre-slice the strawberries and portion the cottage cheese into a pot for 3 days, then assemble in 2 minutes.
💡 Blot the cottage cheese on kitchen paper and spread it only once the toast has cooled and stiffened; warm bread absorbs the whey and turns limp under the strawberries.
Preheat oven to 190°C.
In a skillet, heat olive oil and cook turkey with garlic until browned. Cook until the thickest part reads 74°C.
Stir in rice, tomatoes, spinach, and seasoning; cook 3 more minutes.
Spoon mixture into bell pepper halves and bake for 20 minutes.
💡 Baked peppers keep 4 days chilled and freeze well individually wrapped for 3 months; reheat from chilled at 180°C in the oven or air fryer for 12 minutes, or 800 W for 3 minutes covered.
💡 Roast the empty pepper halves for 10 minutes first so they soften in the bake, and take the turkey off the heat while still moist; it cooks a further 20 minutes and lean mince dries fast.
Preheat oven to 190°C.
Sauté onion and carrot in olive oil for 5 minutes until softened.
Add lentils, tomato paste, broth, thyme, salt, and pepper. Simmer until thick.
Transfer to a baking dish, spread mashed sweet potato on top, and bake for 15 minutes.
💡 Assemble in individual foil trays and chill for 4 days or freeze for 3 months; bake from frozen at 180°C for 35 minutes covered, then uncover for 10 to brown the sweet potato top.
💡 Reduce the lentil base until a spoon dragged through it leaves a clear trail before topping, and mash the sweet potato without added liquid; a wet filling makes the mash slide off and go soggy.
In a jar, mix oats, almond milk, mashed banana, almond butter, vanilla, and chia seeds.
Stir well, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, stir again and add a splash of milk if needed.
Enjoy chilled or slightly warmed for creamy, nutty perfection.
💡 Jars keep 4 days chilled; the banana browns slightly but is fine. To freeze, portion without the banana and stir it in fresh once thawed; warm at 600 W for 90 seconds if you prefer it hot.
💡 Mash the banana completely smooth and whisk it into the almond milk with the almond butter before the oats go in; lumps of banana ferment faster and the almond butter otherwise clings in one clump.
Place banana, eggs, oats, cinnamon, and baking powder in a blender. Blend until smooth and slightly thick.
Warm coconut oil in a nonstick skillet over 175°C.
Pour about 60 ml of batter per pancake and cook for 2–3 minutes, or until bubbles form on the surface.
Flip carefully and cook the other side for another 1–2 minutes until golden brown.
Stack pancakes on a plate and top with your choice of berries, almond butter, or a drizzle of honey.
💡 Stack the cooled pancakes with baking paper between each and chill for up to 3 days, or freeze for 2 months; reheat from frozen in a 180°C air fryer for 3 minutes or a dry pan.
💡 The blended banana-and-egg batter has no flour to hold it, so keep pancakes small and wait for bubbles across the whole surface before flipping, or they will tear.
Cook orzo according to package directions.
In a pan, heat olive oil, sauté garlic and mushrooms for 5 minutes.
Add spinach until wilted.
Stir in cooked orzo, almond milk, and Parmesan until creamy.
Serve immediately.
💡 Keeps 3 days chilled but the orzo drinks the almond milk as it sits, so reheat on the hob with an extra 30 ml of milk or water rather than in the microwave.
💡 Take the pan off the heat before stirring in the Parmesan and almond milk; boiling almond milk with cheese turns grainy, whereas residual heat melts it into a smooth coating.
In a bowl, combine lentils, tomatoes, cucumber, and feta.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper together.
Pour dressing over salad, toss gently, and chill before serving.
💡 Dressed lentils keep 4 days in the fridge and improve overnight; hold back the cucumber and add it on the day so it stays crisp. Do not freeze this salad.
💡 Rinse and drain the cooked lentils thoroughly before dressing, because any clinging cooking liquid dilutes the lemon and oil and leaves the salad tasting flat and watery.
Heat coconut oil in a pot, sauté onion and garlic until soft.
Add lentils, coconut milk, broth, curry powder, and salt.
Simmer for 25 minutes until lentils are soft and creamy.
Serve warm with a sprinkle of herbs.
💡 Portion into tubs and chill for 4 days or freeze for 3 months; red lentils thicken on cooling, so loosen with 50 ml water when reheating in the microwave at 800 W.
💡 Stir the salt in during the last 5 minutes rather than with the broth; seasoning red lentils before they collapse can slow their softening and you lose the creamy texture.
Press tofu gently with a paper towel to remove excess moisture.
Heat sesame oil in a skillet and add tofu cubes. Sauté until golden on each side (about 6–8 minutes).
Add garlic, ginger, and vegetables; stir-fry for 4–5 minutes.
Pour in soy sauce, toss to coat, and cook for 2 more minutes. Serve warm.
💡 Chill for 3 days; the tofu reheats best in an air fryer at 190°C for 4 minutes to crisp back up, while the broccoli goes softer with every microwave blast.
💡 Blotting with kitchen paper is not enough for 200 g of firm tofu; weight it under a plate for 15 minutes, then leave the cubes untouched in the pan until they release themselves.
Cook pasta according to package directions. Reserve 60 ml of the pasta water.
In a blender, combine avocado, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Blend until creamy.
Toss pasta with avocado sauce, adding reserved water to loosen if needed.
Sprinkle with Parmesan (if using) before serving.
💡 This sauce browns within hours, so keep it to 2 days chilled with cling film pressed onto the surface and eat cold or microwave gently at 600 W; never freeze it.
💡 Blend the avocado with the lemon juice first, before the oil, so the acid coats the flesh immediately; add the reserved pasta water in splashes only until the sauce clings rather than pools.
Lay the tortilla flat and spread hummus evenly to cover the surface.
Layer spinach, carrots, cucumber, peppers, and avocado in the center.
Roll the tortilla tightly and slice in half diagonally.
Chill for 10 minutes before serving for a crisp, refreshing bite.
💡 Assembled wraps keep 1 day; for the week, store the cut vegetables and hummus separately and roll each morning, slicing the avocado fresh so it does not brown.
💡 Spread the hummus right to the edges as a moisture barrier, pat the cucumber slices dry on kitchen paper, and lay spinach directly on the hummus so wet vegetables never touch the tortilla.
Toast the bread until golden and crisp.
Spread ricotta evenly over the warm toast.
Drizzle with honey and sprinkle cinnamon on top.
Finish with toasted almond slices for crunch.
Serve immediately with tea or coffee for a cozy morning treat.
💡 Mix the ricotta with the cinnamon and portion into small pots for up to 4 days, keeping the almonds in a jar; toast the bread fresh each morning as it softens within 20 minutes.
💡 Drain watery ricotta in a sieve for 10 minutes before spreading, and toast the almond slices in a dry pan until they smell nutty; raw slices go limp against the soft cheese.
Mash avocado on toasted bread and season with salt and pepper.
Top with roasted chickpeas and drizzle with olive oil.
Sprinkle smoked paprika and enjoy warm or chilled.
💡 Roasted chickpeas lose their crunch in the fridge, so store them at room temperature in a loosely covered jar for 3 days and only mash the avocado just before serving.
💡 Mash the avocado coarsely with a fork rather than blending so it stays thick enough to hold the chickpeas; a squeeze of lemon keeps it green if you prep 30 minutes ahead.
Preheat oven to 165°C.
Toss pumpkin seeds with honey, cinnamon, and salt.
Spread on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Roast 12–15 minutes, stirring once midway.
💡 Cool completely on the tray before jarring, then store airtight at room temperature for 2 weeks; if they soften, re-crisp for 5 minutes at 150°C.
💡 Honey burns before the seeds toast, so spread them in a single layer, stir at the 7 minute mark, and pull them when just golden because they keep darkening on the hot tray.
Combine oats and almond milk in a pot. Bring to a simmer over 175°C and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often.
Add flaxseed, cinnamon, and honey. Mix until smooth and creamy.
Remove from heat and fold in the mixed berries gently.
Serve warm with a few fresh berries on top.
💡 Cooked porridge keeps 4 days chilled; reheat with 40 ml extra almond milk at 700 W, stirring halfway, and fold the berries in after heating so they do not bleed into mush.
💡 Add the flaxseed in the last minute only; stirred in early it thickens the almond milk into a gluey paste before the oats have finished softening.
Preheat your oven to 175°C. Lightly grease a muffin tin with a bit of oil or nonstick spray.
In a bowl, whisk eggs until fluffy. Add salt, pepper, and diced onion.
Fold in the chopped spinach and feta cheese.
Pour the mixture evenly into the muffin cups, filling each about three-quarters full.
Bake for 15–18 minutes or until the tops are set and lightly golden.
Cool slightly before removing. Serve warm or refrigerate for quick breakfasts during the week.
💡 Cool fully, then chill in an airtight box for 4 days or freeze for 2 months; reheat one muffin for 45 seconds at 600 W or in an air fryer at 160°C for 5 minutes.
💡 Squeeze the chopped spinach dry and blot the feta before folding in, then pull the tray at 15 minutes while the centres barely wobble; overbaking makes them rubbery and weepy.
Place the raspberries at the bottom of the blender to start the smooth blending process.
Add Greek yogurt, almond butter, oat milk, and vanilla extract.
Blend on medium for 20–30 seconds to incorporate ingredients, then high for 40–50 seconds until creamy and thick.
Check the texture — add a small splash of oat milk if you want a lighter consistency.
Pour into glasses and enjoy a creamy pink drink rich with antioxidants.
💡 Freeze prepped pouches of raspberries, yogurt and almond butter; on the day, blend with the oat milk and whey for a shake ready within 40 minutes of finishing your session.
💡 Load in this order: oat milk, whey, yogurt, almond butter, then frozen raspberries on top; the almond butter needs liquid around it or it clings to the blade unmixed.
Toss greens with roasted beets, goat cheese, and walnuts in a bowl.
Drizzle olive oil and balsamic vinegar over the top.
Gently toss and serve immediately for best flavor and color.
💡 Keep the roasted beets, greens and crumbled goat cheese in separate compartments for up to 4 days; beets stain everything pink within hours once combined.
💡 Dress and toss the greens first, then scatter beets, walnuts and cheese on top rather than tossing everything together, or the goat cheese smears and the walnuts soften.
Combine oats, coconut milk, chia seeds, and honey in a jar.
Stir well, seal, and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, top with mango and shredded coconut.
Stir and enjoy cool — tropical, creamy, and sunshine-sweet.
💡 Make up to 4 jars at once for 4 days chilled; add the mango and shredded coconut each morning, and freeze diced mango in 41 g portions to keep it firm.
💡 Shake the coconut milk tin well and stir the jar again after 10 minutes, otherwise the chia seeds sink and set into a rubbery layer at the bottom.
In a skillet, heat olive oil and sauté garlic for 1 minute.
Add cooked quinoa and stir for 2 minutes.
Add broccoli and cheddar, mixing until the cheese melts evenly.
Season with salt and pepper, then serve warm.
💡 Portion while warm and chill for 4 days; freezes for 2 months. Reheat at 700 W with a spoon of water and stir halfway to melt the cheddar evenly.
💡 Use quinoa that has cooled and dried out slightly; freshly cooked quinoa straight from the pan is too wet and turns the cheddar into a stringy clump rather than a light coating.
Arrange grain, chickpeas, and vegetables in a bowl.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, and water into a smooth dressing.
Drizzle over bowl and serve warm or cold.
💡 Grains and roasted vegetables keep 4 days chilled; keep the tahini dressing in a separate pot as it thickens when cold, then whisk with 5 ml of warm water before serving.
💡 Do not panic when the tahini clumps as the lemon goes in; keep whisking and add the warm water 5 ml at a time and it will loosen into a smooth pourable dressing.
Rinse quinoa under cold water. Combine with almond milk in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until fluffy.
Stir in honey and cinnamon, then remove from heat.
Divide between bowls and top with almonds, walnuts, and banana slices.
Serve warm with an extra drizzle of honey if desired.
💡 Cooked quinoa porridge keeps 4 days chilled; reheat with 30 ml almond milk at 700 W, adding the nuts and banana after warming so the nuts stay crunchy.
💡 Rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve until the water runs clear to wash off the bitter saponin coating, and keep the lid on for a 5 minute rest after simmering for fluffy grains.
Place strawberries and kiwi in the blender first to create a colorful base.
Add Greek yogurt and almond milk. Blend on medium for 20–30 seconds, then high until creamy and smooth.
Taste and add honey for extra sweetness if desired, blending briefly to combine.
Pour into glasses and enjoy the vibrant, antioxidant-rich smoothie immediately.
💡 Kiwi turns bitter after blending and standing, so drink within 15 minutes; prep only the strawberries and kiwi in freezer bags and blend fresh after training.
💡 Pour the almond milk in first, pulse the whey in briefly, then add yogurt and fruit; peel the kiwi properly because the skin gives green flecks and a fuzzy texture.
Heat olive oil in a pot and sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add carrots and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in chickpeas, tomatoes, broth, and all spices.
Simmer for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally until thickened.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve with couscous or rice.
💡 Chill in tubs for 5 days or freeze for 3 months; it thickens overnight, so reheat on the hob with a splash of broth and cook couscous separately on the day.
💡 Add the cinnamon and cumin to the oil with the onion for 30 seconds before the liquid goes in; blooming them removes the raw, dusty taste stirring them into broth leaves.
In a bowl, whisk yogurt, peanut butter, and honey until creamy.
Serve as a dip with your choice of fresh fruit.
Keep refrigerated for up to two days.
💡 Portion into 70 g pots and keep chilled for 2 days; cut fruit stored alongside should be apple or pear tossed in lemon, as berries leak juice into the dip.
💡 Loosen the peanut butter by stirring a spoonful of the yogurt into it before adding the rest; tipping it straight in leaves stubborn lumps that never whisk out.
Place the frozen strawberries in the blender first so they break down easily.
Add the sliced peach, Greek yogurt, and almond milk.
Blend on high for 30–40 seconds until the mixture becomes velvety and uniform in color.
Pause to scrape down the sides if needed, ensuring all fruit is fully incorporated.
Add the honey and give it one final blend to softly sweeten and bring the flavors together.
If it feels too thick, add a splash more almond milk and blend again for a smoother pour.
💡 Freeze sliced peach alongside the strawberries in single portions; the finished smoothie is then thick enough to hold for 30 minutes in a bottle after training without separating.
💡 Two frozen fruits can stall a small blender, so blend the almond milk, whey and yogurt smooth first, then add the frozen fruit and pulse before running on high.
Add mango and Greek yogurt to the blender first for a smooth base.
Add kale and coconut water. Blend on medium to start breaking down the greens.
Add ginger and increase speed to high until smooth and silky.
Pour into glasses and enjoy a vitamin-rich, energizing smoothie.
💡 Freeze mango and kale together in bags, then blend on the morning of training with the coconut water; drink within 30 minutes as the kale turns grassy on standing.
💡 Blend the kale with the coconut water alone for 30 seconds until no flecks remain, then add whey, yogurt and mango; adding the greens last leaves stringy bits.
Add cucumber and mint leaves to the blender first for a fresh base.
Pour in Greek yogurt and coconut water. Blend on medium for 20–30 seconds.
Increase to high speed and blend until creamy and fully combined.
Add ice and blend briefly to chill.
Pour into glasses and enjoy a cooling, refreshing smoothie.
💡 Lowest in carbs of the range, so it suits a rest day or an evening drink; blend fresh, as cucumber releases water and the yogurt separates within an hour of standing.
💡 Add the ice last and pulse only 3 or 4 times; over-blending ice with cucumber turns the drink thin and watery, and bruises the mint into bitterness.
Add blueberries and banana into the blender first to form a colorful base.
Pour in Greek yogurt and coconut water. Blend on medium to combine.
Increase speed to high and blend until smooth and creamy.
Taste and add honey for extra sweetness if desired, blending briefly.
Pour into glasses and enjoy the calming blueberry flavor.
💡 Freeze the blueberries and banana together in a bag so no ice is needed; blended the night before, it keeps 12 hours in a sealed jar for a post-training drink.
💡 Blend the coconut water and whey first for 10 seconds, then add yogurt, banana and blueberries; the banana should be spotted and ripe or the smoothie tastes starchy.
Place peaches and raspberries into the blender first.
Add Greek yogurt, protein powder, and almond milk. Blend on medium to start combining.
Increase to high speed and blend until creamy and smooth.
Taste and adjust sweetness if desired.
Pour into glasses and enjoy a protein-rich, fruity smoothie.
💡 Freeze the peach slices and raspberries in bags; with only 15 g of powder here, drink it alongside a proper meal rather than as your sole post-training protein.
💡 Whisk the protein powder into the almond milk in the blender jug before any fruit; raspberry seeds and powder clumps together make a gritty drink if added at the same time.
Add all berries and banana to the blender first to form a fruity base.
Pour in Greek yogurt and almond milk. Blend on medium to combine ingredients.
Increase speed to high until smooth and creamy.
Taste and adjust sweetness if desired.
Pour into glasses and enjoy a comforting, antioxidant-rich smoothie.
💡 Bag up 105 g fruit portions and freeze; blend on the day and drink within 45 minutes of training, or chill in a sealed bottle for up to 8 hours and shake.
💡 Two berries plus banana make a thick blend that can trap air pockets; stop after 20 seconds, scrape the sides and give it a second run on high.
Heat olive oil in a pot; sauté onion, garlic, and mushrooms until golden.
Add lentils, thyme, paprika, and broth.
Simmer 30 minutes until lentils are soft and broth thickens slightly.
Serve warm with a drizzle of olive oil or herbs.
💡 Cool and chill for 5 days or freeze flat in bags for 3 months; brown lentils absorb broth overnight, so reheat on the hob with 50 ml water and a fresh drizzle of oil.
💡 Cook the mushrooms until properly golden before adding liquid, then keep the pot at a steady low simmer; brown lentils boiled hard split their skins and turn mushy.
Add peaches and mango to the blender first for a fruit-forward base.
Pour in orange juice and Greek yogurt.
Blend on medium for 20–30 seconds, then high until creamy and smooth.
Taste and add honey if additional sweetness is desired.
Pour immediately and enjoy a bright, vitamin C–rich smoothie.
💡 Highest carb smoothie here, so it fits best in the hour after a hard session; freeze peach and mango in 118 g bags and pour the orange juice in first on the day.
💡 Orange juice and Greek yogurt can turn grainy if blended too long at high speed; blend the whey into the juice first, then add yogurt and fruit and stop as soon as it is smooth.
Heat olive oil, sauté garlic until fragrant.
Add tomatoes, chickpeas, and curry powder; simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk and spinach; cook until wilted.
Serve warm with brown rice or flatbread.
💡 Keeps 4 days chilled and freezes for 3 months; add the spinach fresh when reheating rather than freezing it, and warm at 700 W with the lid ajar to stop coconut milk spitting.
💡 Stir the coconut milk in over low heat and never let it boil hard afterwards; light coconut milk splits into oily flecks when boiled, and a gentle simmer is enough to wilt spinach.
Heat olive oil in a pot; sauté onion and garlic until fragrant.
Add lentils, broth, carrots, celery, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25– 30 minutes until lentils are tender.
Serve warm with a drizzle of olive oil if desired.
💡 Portion into tubs, chill for 5 days or freeze for 3 months; it sets firm when cold, so loosen with 60 ml broth on the hob, stirring so the base does not catch.
💡 Dice the carrot and celery to the size of a lentil so everything is tender at the same time; big chunks are still crunchy when the lentils are already collapsing.
Add the oats to the blender first so they break down easily.
Pour in the almond milk to create a soft base for the oats.
Add peaches, banana, honey, and ice.
Blend on high for 60–75 seconds until the oats dissolve into a creamy, comforting texture.
If you want it thinner, add more almond milk and blend briefly again.
💡 Soak the oats in the almond milk overnight in the blender jug in the fridge; in the morning add whey, fruit and ice and it blends smoother and fuels a morning session.
💡 Add the oats and almond milk first and run 20 seconds alone until milky; adding ice at the same time keeps the oats coarse and the drink gritty.
Heat sesame oil in a skillet. Sauté garlic and veggies for 2 minutes.
Add cauliflower rice and cook for 5 minutes.
Push mixture aside, scramble egg, then mix everything together.
Stir in soy sauce and garnish with green onions.
💡 Good for 3 days in the fridge; reheat in a hot dry pan or air fryer at 200°C for 4 minutes to drive off moisture, because microwaving makes cauliflower rice steam and turn soggy.
💡 Cook the cauliflower rice in a wide pan without crowding so it fries rather than steams, and scramble the egg in a cleared space until just set before folding through.
In a small bowl, mix the yogurt with the lemon juice, chili flakes, and a pinch of salt, stirring until the flavors blend into a smooth, tangy dip.
Serve the mixture with crisp carrot sticks, letting each dip pick up a little heat and brightness for a refreshing, satisfying snack.
💡 Mixed dip keeps 4 days chilled; store carrot sticks in a tub of cold water, changed daily, so they stay snappy for 5 days and are not stored touching the dip.
💡 Stir the lemon juice in a few drops at a time; 2.5 ml is plenty, and more thins the Greek yogurt into a runny sauce that slides off the carrot.
Mix tuna, mashed avocado, Greek yogurt, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Season with salt and pepper.
Toast the bread slices and spread the mixture evenly on top.
Serve immediately with a sprinkle of chili flakes (optional).
💡 The tuna mix keeps 2 days chilled in a sealed pot with cling film on the surface; toast the bread fresh each time and never freeze, as the avocado turns grey.
💡 Drain the tuna hard by pressing it against the tin lid, and mash the avocado separately before folding through; wet tuna turns the yogurt binder into a puddle.
Thread a tomato, basil leaf, and mozzarella ball onto each skewer.
Drizzle olive oil and balsamic glaze over the top.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.
💡 Assemble up to 2 days ahead and chill in a sealed box; add the basil and oil on the day, as basil blackens in the fridge, and rest at room temperature for 15 minutes before eating.
💡 Pat the mozzarella balls dry on kitchen paper before threading, or the brine mixes with the oil and puddles under the skewers; tear basil rather than chopping it to limit bruising.
Add the tofu cubes to a bowl and drizzle them with the olive oil and soy sauce.
Sprinkle the garlic powder over the top, then toss everything together until each cube is evenly coated and lightly seasoned.
Arrange the tofu pieces in a single layer in your air fryer basket and cook at 190°C for 10–12 minutes, shaking the basket halfway through to help them crisp evenly on all sides.
Serve the tofu hot and golden with your favorite dipping sauce for a cozy, satisfying snack.
💡 Keeps chilled 4 days in a lidded tub; refresh in the air fryer at 190°C for 3–4 minutes rather than the microwave, which turns the crust leathery. Not worth freezing.
💡 Press the tofu between kitchen paper under a weighted plate for 15 minutes before cubing; wet tofu steams in the basket and never crisps.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Blend chickpeas, garlic, parsley, olive oil, flour, cumin, and salt in a food processor until coarse.
Form small balls and place on a lined baking sheet.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, flipping halfway through.
Serve with a side of mixed greens or yogurt dip.
💡 Baked falafel keeps 4 days chilled and freezes for 3 months once cooled; reheat from frozen in an air fryer at 180°C for 8 minutes, storing greens and yogurt dip separately.
💡 Drain and blot the chickpeas thoroughly and pulse rather than purée; a coarse, crumbly mix holds its shape, whereas a smooth paste spreads flat and stays pasty inside.
Preheat oven to 190°C.
Sauté tomatoes and spinach in olive oil for 3 minutes.
Mix with quinoa, feta, salt, and pepper.
Spoon mixture into bell peppers and bake for 20 minutes.
Serve warm with a squeeze of lemon.
💡 Assembled peppers keep 4 days chilled and freeze well for 2 months; reheat covered in the microwave at 700 W for 3 minutes, adding the lemon squeeze only at the table.
💡 Cook the tomatoes down until almost dry before folding in the quinoa; excess liquid pools in the pepper base and leaves the filling waterlogged.
Preheat oven to 190°C. Scoop out eggplant flesh and chop it finely.
Sauté chopped eggplant and garlic in olive oil for 5 minutes.
Mix with quinoa, tomatoes, spinach, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Spoon filling into eggplant shells and bake for 20 minutes.
💡 Chill the filled boats for up to 3 days; reheat uncovered in the oven at 180°C for 12 minutes so the shells firm up rather than turning mushy. Freezing softens the eggplant too far.
💡 Salt the scooped shells and leave them cut-side down for 10 minutes, then pat dry; this draws out bitter moisture and stops the boats collapsing in the oven.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Brush eggplant slices with olive oil, sprinkle breadcrumbs, and bake 15 minutes.
Layer with marinara and cheese; bake another 10 minutes.
Serve warm with a side salad.
💡 Layered portions keep 3 days chilled; reheat in the air fryer at 180°C for 6 minutes to revive the breadcrumb crust, since a microwave will soften it. It freezes for 2 months.
💡 Give the oiled slices the full 15 minutes alone before adding marinara; undercooked eggplant releases water beneath the sauce and the whole tray goes soggy.
Preheat oven to 175°C and line a muffin tin with paper liners.
In a mixing bowl, whisk eggs, honey, almond milk, and vanilla until combined.
Add almond flour, oats, and baking powder; mix into a thick batter.
Gently fold in blueberries.
Spoon the batter into muffin cups, filling each about ¾ full.
Bake for 18–20 minutes or until golden brown and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool slightly before serving.
💡 Store in an airtight tin for 3 days or freeze individually wrapped for 3 months; 20 seconds at 800 W brings a frozen muffin back to soft and warm.
💡 Toss the blueberries in 2.5 g of the almond flour before folding; the coating stops them sinking to the base of the dense almond batter.
Heat olive oil in a pan, sauté garlic and veggies until slightly tender.
Add cooked quinoa and soy sauce, stirring well.
Sprinkle sesame seeds and serve warm.
💡 Portion into tubs and chill for up to 4 days; reheat in a hot wok or pan with a splash of water for 3 minutes rather than microwaving, which makes the vegetables limp.
💡 Use quinoa that has been cooked and cooled beforehand, ideally from the fridge; freshly cooked grains steam and clump, while chilled ones fry loose and separate.
Blend banana, spinach, almond milk, matcha powder, and almond butter until creamy.
Pour into a bowl and top with granola.
Enjoy immediately for an energizing, antioxidant-rich start to your day.
💡 Freeze the blended base in silicone muffin moulds, then thaw two pucks in the fridge overnight and stir; keep the granola in a dry jar until serving. The blend keeps only 24 hours chilled.
💡 Whisk the matcha into the almond milk first and use frozen banana slices; whole matcha powder clumps in a thick blend and warm banana gives a runny bowl.
Roast sweet potato cubes with olive oil, cumin, salt, and pepper for 20 minutes at 205°C.
In a bowl, combine lentils and spinach. Add roasted sweet potatoes.
Drizzle with extra olive oil and toss to mix.
💡 Both components chill for 4 days; store the roasted sweet potato and lentils in one tub but add the spinach fresh each day. Reheat at 800 W for 2 minutes.
💡 Simmer the dried lentils in unsalted water for 18–20 minutes until just tender, then drain immediately; overcooked lentils collapse into a paste that hides the roasted cubes.
